before.summary: Accelerate Resources has compiled historical RAB and re-evaluated its own 2021–2023 RC drilling at the Woodie Woodie North Manganese Project, revealing multiple near-surface intercepts exceeding 50% manganese. These results validate high-grade corridors including El Largo and Area 42, supporting the potential for direct-shipping-ore style mineralisation ahead of a targeted mid-year RC drill program. All intersections are reported as down-hole lengths and true widths are not currently known.
before.grade_commentary: Manganese grades above 44% Mn are generally considered high-grade and potentially direct-shipping-ore (DSO) quality depending on impurities; intercepts up to 50.8% Mn are exceptional. However, many high-grade intervals are narrow (1–2m) and reported as down-hole lengths with true widths currently unknown, meaning selective mining or further delineation would be required.

before.context: Broad shallow intercepts of 1–1.8 g/t Au over 8–28m are consistent with early-stage Yilgarn greenstone-hosted orogenic gold exploration in the Kalgoorlie district, where initial aircore programs typically target shallow oxide zones ahead of RC drilling; the 300m strike length and multi-hole continuity is encouraging at this stage.
before.grade_commentary: Grades of 1.01g/t Au (28m) and included intervals up to 1.78g/t Au (8m) are low-moderate for orogenic gold in the Kalgoorlie region, but the broad widths and shallow depth (from 16–36m) are positive for open-pit exploration potential. Estimated true width is not explicitly quantified; however, drilling is interpreted to be roughly perpendicular to strike, suggesting down-hole widths approximate true widths. Mineralisation is open down-dip and along strike.
before.key_facts: ["26BGAC039 returned a broad shallow intercept of 28m @ 1.01g/t Au from 36m, including two higher-grade zones of 8m @ 1.78g/t Au from 40m and 8m @ 1.37g/t Au from 52m — the 1.78g/t interval is well above typical broad aircore background for this district.","Multiple holes reported multiple significant intercepts: 26BGAC043 returned 20m @ 0.76g/t Au incl. 8m @ 1.42g/t Au from 28m alongside separate intervals of 4m @ 0.21g/t Au and 3m @ 0.25g/t Au; 26BGAC044 returned 8m @ 0.62g/t Au from 48m and 4m @ 0.44g/t Au from 68m; and 26BGAC009 returned 4m @ 1.75g/t Au from 32m along the Paris Gift trend extension.","The Spencers Prospect defines a coherent ~300m north-south shallow mineralised structure on newly acquired tenement M25/92, open down-dip and along strike, representing the second new trend discovered at Balagundi since late 2025."]

before.summary: Aguia Resources has significantly improved head grades at its Santa Barbara gold mine in Colombia, with the final April production batch achieving an estimated 12 g/t Au head grade and 10.31 g/t Au recovered — roughly triple the 3–4 g/t average of prior months. The improvement follows implementation of optimized narrow-vein mining methods and tighter grade control. However, total April ore production was just 80 tonnes, with the first batch from oxidized upper Stope 1 permanently abandoned.
before.context: The Santa Barbara project was added via Aguia's acquisition of Andean Mining, and the company explicitly states there are no JORC Mineral Resource Estimates for any Colombian asset. While 10–12 g/t Au is bonanza grade for narrow-vein underground mining, the 80-tonne monthly scale is pilot-level output and the mine plan lacks defined reserves.
before.grade_commentary: 10–12 g/t Au is bonanza grade and excellent for narrow-vein selective mining. The prior 3–4 g/t Au reflected heavy dilution; the new grades demonstrate improved mining discipline rather than new geology. The filing does not report specific true widths for individual production faces, though JORC Table 1 notes true thickness is generally 60–70% of sampled thickness.
before.key_facts: ["Head grades improved from a 3–4 g/t Au average to an estimated 12 g/t Au (before losses) in the final April batch, with total recovery of 10.31 g/t Au — a roughly 3x improvement.","Total ore production in April was only 80 tonnes, and the first batch mined from oxidized upper Stope 1 was permanently abandoned.","Development is advancing on Vein #2 and two shafts have been sunk beneath Vein #1 to access lower sublevels, targeting higher-grade zones identified in prior drilling."]

before.summary: Alara Resources released a revised investor presentation for the Paydirt Conference to include compliance disclosures for the historic Daris East Mineral Resource Estimate. The deposit holds a Measured and Indicated resource of 240,024 tonnes grading 2.37% copper — nearly triple the head grade at the producing Al Wash-hi Majaza mine — though it has not been updated from the original 2004 JORC standard. The presentation also notes FY26 Q3 production beat plan by 12%, producing 10,782 DMT of copper concentrate.
before.context: The 2.37% Cu grade at Daris East is considered high-grade by global standards and compares favourably to the 0.86–0.88% Cu feed currently processed at Al Wash-hi Majaza, suggesting potential for higher-margin satellite feed. However, the 240,024-tonne resource is small and remains a historic JORC 2004 estimate, meaning it lacks modern data verification and has not been subject to updated technical or economic studies.
before.grade_commentary: 2.37% Cu is a high-grade copper resource, well above the 1.5% threshold and nearly three times the 0.86–0.88% Cu mill feed grade at the operating Al Wash-hi Majaza mine. While the grade is exceptional, the modest 240kt tonnage and lack of width or depth data in the presentation mean investors should treat this as a small, high-grade satellite target pending modern verification.
before.key_facts: ["Daris East hosts a Measured and Indicated resource of 240,024 tonnes at 2.37% Cu (2.48% Cu Measured), a grade nearly 3x higher than the Al Wash-hi Majaza mill feed of 0.86–0.88% Cu.","FY26 Q3 production exceeded plan by 12%: 296,439 tonnes of ore processed and 10,782 DMT of copper concentrate produced.","The Daris East resource was originally reported under JORC Code 2004 and has not been updated to JORC 2012; the presentation was revised solely to add this compliance disclosure."]

before.grade_commentary: The 2.67% Sr (4.49% SrCO₃) head grade is exceptionally high for carbonatite-hosted strontium mineralisation, and the 98.96% extraction at ambient temperature is outstanding—exceeding typical 80–95% recoveries reported for strontianite/ancylite systems and eliminating the need for the energy-intensive pyrometallurgical routes required for conventional celestite ores.
before.key_facts: ["98.96% strontium extraction achieved in HCl acid leach at ambient temperature (~21°C) from composite sample grading 2.67% Sr (4.49% SrCO₃) and 12.70% Ca — among the highest reported globally for any strontium-bearing ore system under comparable conditions.","Existing Inferred Mineral Resource of 520.61 Mt at 2.49% TREO equivalent (announced 26 Sept 2025); updated MRE accelerated to incorporate SrCO₃ and Fe content from Phase 1 drilling.","Phase 2 drilling is complete with assay results for 10 holes still pending; strontium carbonate prices have surged ~150% to US$3,150/tonne (CFR Europe) amid severe supply disruptions."]

before.grade_commentary: The 0.76% Nb₂O₅ intercept is exceptional for primary hard-rock niobium (global producers such as Niobec report mill feed grades nearer 0.5–0.6% Nb₂O₅), while the 2.94% TREO and 7.64% SrCO₃ are bonanza-level values for a carbonatite REE-Sr system. However, all widths reported are downhole lengths; true widths have not been established, meaning the actual horizontal thickness could differ materially.
before.key_facts: ["DD003A returned an exceptional 11m at 0.76% Nb₂O₅ from 102m — a standout grade for primary hard-rock niobium — alongside a near-surface bonanza intercept of 5m at 2.94% TREO and 7.64% SrCO₃ from 64m, both well above typical carbonatite norms.","DD003A contained multiple threshold-exceeding intercepts in a single hole: 11m at 0.76% Nb₂O₅, 5.8m at 0.43% Nb₂O₅, 31m at 0.32% Nb₂O₅, and 5m at 2.94% TREO with 7.64% SrCO₃, establishing the northern flank as a genuine multi-commodity domain.","DD018A confirmed 74m of cumulative stacked mineralisation on the southern margin — including a 51m lower layer at 0.70% TREO and 0.32% Nb₂O₅ — proving the carbonatite stratigraphy extends robustly southward and remains open along strike and at depth."]

before.grade_commentary: The 0.41% Nb₂O₅ over 19m is moderate to good for carbonatite-hosted niobium, approaching the approximate mined grades at the comparable Niobec operation in Canada. The 1.58% TREO and 1.39% TREO intercepts are moderate for REE carbonatites, and while the 5–7m widths are narrower than the central core, they remain amenable to bulk mining methods if the geometry holds. These results represent the outer edge of the mineralised envelope, not the high-grade heart.

before.summary: Alice Queen Limited lodged a supplementary prospectus for its ongoing rights issue, adding a detailed use-of-funds table and updated director interest disclosures. The company aims to raise up to $5.77 million, with more than half directed to Horn Island diamond core drilling, and expects the proceeds to fund roughly 12 months of operations. Major shareholder Gage — associated with director Jianying Wang — has committed to take up its entitlement and sub-underwrite shortfall shares, potentially lifting its stake to a maximum 51% post-issue.

before.summary: Alice Queen Limited (ASX: AQX) has amended its 28 April 2026 Horn Island Exploration Target announcement to add a 3D sectional view (Figure 2) and clarify data footnotes in Appendices 2 and 5. The underlying exploration target ranges are unchanged, outlining conceptual hard-rock potential of 34.6–52.0 Mt @ 0.88–1.32 g/t Au for 1.22–1.83 Moz, plus surface stockpiles, tailings and alluvial material of 25.1–37.6 Mt @ 0.31–0.46 g/t Au for 0.31–0.46 Moz. The Company notes the target is conceptual in nature and there has been insufficient exploration to estimate a JORC Mineral Resource.
before.ticker_summary: AQX amends Horn Island ET announcement; adds figure, footnotes. No change to 1.5–2.3Moz conceptual target.
before.context: The Horn Island conceptual target represents a potential 3×–4× uplift over the existing 2021 JORC resource of 524 koz @ 0.98 g/t Au. Exploration targets around historic open-pit mines are common in the Australian gold sector, but conversion to a JORC resource depends heavily on infill drilling and QAQC validation — notably, the company flags historic drill data as incomplete and subject to ongoing validation.
before.grade_commentary: The overall hard-rock ET grade of 0.88–1.32 g/t Au is low-moderate for an intrusion-related vein system and sits at the margins of typical open-pit economics without exceptional width or metallurgy. However, the Cable Bay Prospect sub-range of 1.47–2.20 g/t Au is high-moderate to high grade relative to the existing 0.98 g/t MRE and could support more selective mining scenarios if continuity is proven. The stockpile/alluvial domain at 0.31–0.46 g/t Au is low grade but potentially viable given its at-surface nature.
before.key_facts: ["The Cable Bay hard-rock subdomain carries an exploration target of 4.8–7.1 Mt grading 1.47–2.20 g/t Au — more than double the existing Horn Island MRE grade of 0.98 g/t Au and the highest-grade component of the new target.","Historical diamond drill hole 20NGD105 returned multiple high-grade intercepts within the Resource Extension area, including 1m @ 12.4 g/t Au from 244m and 2m @ 3.9 g/t Au incl. 1m @ 5.4 g/t Au from 355m, supporting the domain's grade potential.","The combined hard-rock and surface/alluvial exploration target outlines conceptual upside of 1.53–2.29 Moz Au — roughly 3× to 4.4× the existing 524 koz JORC resource — but remains conceptual with no guarantee of conversion to a Mineral Resource."]

before.context: Historic small-scale gold mines in the Yilgarn Craton often produced high-grade pods at 28–78 g/t Au from small stopes, and first-pass RC programs targeting broader envelopes typically return moderate grades like these 3 g/t Au intercepts until higher-grade shoots are located with infill drilling.
before.grade_commentary: 3.2 g/t Au over ~2.55–2.85m estimated true width (85–95% of 3m downhole) is moderate grade and respectable for shallow Archean orogenic gold, though well below the historic production grades of 28–78 g/t. The internal 1m @ 8.1 g/t is high-grade but not bonanza (>10 g/t). These widths are sufficient to be economic if continuity is proven, but the intercepts are from a very small first-pass program and remain open in all directions.

before.summary: Altair Minerals announced bonanza-grade grab samples of up to 34.56 g/t Au from the first deep trench at its South Oko (SOKO) project in Guyana, indicating primary gold mineralisation exists below the laterite duricrust. A Pole-Dipole IP survey also defined several large chargeability structures, including Structure M which measures ~150–250 m in width and extends over ~2.5 km of strike, remaining open to the south. Separately, infill and step-out diamond drilling is scheduled to begin this week at the North Peters target.
before.key_facts: ["Grab samples from the base of SOKO Trench 6 — the first deep trench (~6 m) to penetrate the laterite duricrust — returned 34.56 g/t Au and 27.21 g/t Au from exposed quartz veins in saprolite, providing direct evidence of primary mineralisation below the leached cover.","Pole-Dipole IP modelling identified four deep-tapping chargeability structures at SOKO, including Structure M (~150–250 m wide, ~2.5 km strike, open to the south) and Structure N (~100–250 m wide, ~600 m strike, coincident with a gold-in-soil anomaly).","Diamond drilling at North Peters is scheduled to commence this week following 28 step-out RAB holes, while assays from over 400 soil samples, 200 auger holes and 1.5 km of trenching at SOKO remain pending."]

before.summary: Altitude Minerals has secured an exclusive eight-year option to purchase the W-Project, a low-sulphidation epithermal gold-silver property near Winnemucca, Nevada. Historical drilling from the 1980s–1990s returned widespread near-surface gold, including 37m @ 1.30 g/t Au and 3m @ 3.75 g/t Au, but the data lacks modern QA/QC and the high-grade boiling-zone feeders remain untested. The company plans geophysical surveys in 2026 and aims to be drill-ready by Autumn 2026, with potential to combine field programs with its nearby Firenze Project.
before.context: The W-Project lies on the western margin of the Northern Nevada Rift, adjacent to the Battle Mountain–Eureka Trend, in the same district as the Sleeper (0.36 g/t Au) and Sandman (0.73 g/t Au) deposits. Historical drilling averaged only 72–258m depth and focused on a shallow quartz/calcite vein, leaving deeper high-grade structures analogous to the nearby Midas Mine (~15.5 g/t AuEq historical production) completely untested.
before.key_facts: ["Historical hole W87-1 returned 37m @ 1.30 g/t Au incl. 15m @ 2.19 g/t Au, and W87-6 returned 3m @ 3.75 g/t Au — multiples of the nearby Sleeper (0.36 g/t Au) and Sandman (0.73 g/t Au) resource grades","40 of 43 historical drill holes intersected gold mineralisation and 7 ended in mineralisation, leaving targets open at depth; the project has seen no systematic modern exploration","Staged option terms total US$490k cash + US$500k in shares over 8 years plus US$1.2m work commitments, with a 3% NSR (2% buydown for US$2m) — low cost preserves treasury"]

before.summary: Antares Metals has secured A$237,500 in non-dilutive Western Australian government funding to co-fund RC and diamond drilling plus a high-resolution aeromagnetic survey at its Quinns copper-zinc-gold VMS project. The filing highlights several shallow, high-grade historic intersections — notably 2m @ 16.9% Cu and 2m @ 45.6% Zn in hole 10ATD001 — that were excluded from the project’s 1.48Mt JORC 2004 resource. AM5 is targeting a maiden JORC 2012 resource at Austin and expects EIS-funded drilling to commence in Q3 2026, while a 1,000m program at Conglomerate Creek (Qld) is set to begin in the coming weeks.
before.grade_commentary: The historic intercepts of 10.2%–16.9% Cu and 33.3%–45.6% Zn are exceptional massive sulphide grades far above the Austin resource average of 1.02% Cu and 1.39% Zn, and would be considered bonanza-grade in any VMS setting. True widths are not reported, but the drilled widths (2m–6m for the ultra-high-grade intervals) imply narrow, selective lenses within broader envelopes (58m @ 2.0% Cu, 38m @ 14% Zn); if these prove continuous they could materially lift project economics.
before.what_to_watch: Maiden EIS-funded RC drilling at Quinns is targeted for Q3 2026 — monitor for heritage survey completion and drill permitting. Near-term catalysts include the 1,000m Conglomerate Creek (Qld) drilling program commencing in the coming weeks, and whether AM5’s Q3 drilling tests the deeper ~450m extensions where historical Silver Swan holes identified additional Cu-Zn mineralisation below the 2004 resource.

However, the shallow intercepts (1–7m) in flat-lying paleochannel conglomerate show strong gravity upgradability, with concentrate grades of 0.46–4.5 g/t Au and concentration factors up to 22.6x. before.grade_commentary: The 5B deposit carries an Inferred resource of 4.2 g/t Au, so intercepts grading 29.1 g/t Au, 13.4 g/t Au and 10.3 g/t Au are bonanza grades (>10 g/t Au) that represent multiples of the resource grade. These ultra-high-grade intervals occur over narrow 1–2 metre widths within broader 4–9 metre zones of moderate mineralisation. Results are reported as downhole lengths; drilling is oriented normal to the interpreted north-south strike and 65° west dip, suggesting widths approximate true widths, though ETW is not explicitly stated. Mineralisation at 5B remains open down-dip, with deeper historical intersections in the shear assayed only for nickel, not gold.
before.key_facts: ["RC hole SGRC154 intersected 1m at 29.1 g/t Au within 4m at 8.31 g/t Au — nearly 7 times the 5B Inferred resource grade of 4.2 g/t Au","RC hole SGRC144 returned 1m at 13.4 g/t Au, more than 3 times the 5B deposit resource grade","RC hole SGRC148 returned 2m at 10.3 g/t Au within 9m at 4.38 g/t Au — a bonanza-grade interval more than 2.4 times the 5B resource grade"]

before.grade_commentary: For sandstone-hosted uranium, 673ppm eU₃O₈ is exceptional — more than triple the existing Chisebuka resource grade of 220ppm and well above the ~300–400ppm typical of many operating mines globally. The thick, near-surface widths (up to 24m from <35m depth) are highly favourable, and true width is approximately equal to drilled width given vertical holes intercept shallow 15° dipping mineralisation. However, grades are derived from down-hole gamma probe measurements (eU₃O₈) and have not yet been verified by chemical assay, which remains a standard next step for resource confidence.
before.key_facts: ["CHDTH2193 returned 12.7m at 673ppm eU₃O₈ from 18.0m depth — more than 3x the existing Chisebuka Inferred resource grade of 220ppm.","CHDTH2192 returned two exceptional near-surface intercepts in one hole: 24.0m at 448ppm eU₃O₈ from 32.2m and 15.9m at 361ppm eU₃O₈ from 4.7m, both substantially exceeding the 220ppm resource grade.","The new SW higher-grade zone now spans 600m x 300m and is drilled to the density required for Mineral Resource estimation, with two rigs continuing to test extensions."]

before.summary: Atomic Eagle has signed a binding option to acquire the 429 km² Sitwe Uranium Project in Zambia’s Luangwa Valley, expanding its national tenement footprint by 38%. The project includes encouraging historical shallow RC intercepts such as 1,620 ppm U₃O₈ over 1m and 735 ppm U₃O₈ over 6m from seven holes drilled in 2010–2012, with mineralisation open at depth and along strike. The deal requires US$200,000 in exploration spending by mid-2027 to earn the right to purchase the licence for US$400,000.
before.key_facts: ["Historic intercepts include 1,620 ppm U3O8 over 1m (STN001) and 1,080 ppm over 1m (STN002), exceeding the Muntanga resource grade of 359 ppm U3O8 by more than 4x and 3x, respectively; STN003 also returned 6m at 735 ppm U3O8.","Multiple significant intercepts were reported in single holes: STN003 returned four shallow hits including 5m at 566 ppm, 2m at 636 ppm and 6m at 735 ppm, while STN002 returned two intercepts of 2m at 639 ppm and 1m at 1,080 ppm; reported widths are approximately 20% greater than true width.","Low-cost option to earn 100% requires US$200,000 in exploration expenditure by 30 June 2027 plus a US$400,000 exercise price, adding 429 km² and boosting Atomic Eagle’s Zambian holdings by 38%."]

before.summary: AuKing Mining has completed a drone-based magnetic and LiDAR survey covering the 5 km Tundulu carbonatite complex in Malawi, with processed data expected within 7–10 days to refine Rare Earth Element drill targets. The company is engaging drilling contractors and local communities with the aim of commencing a maiden drill program in May. This marks the first fieldwork since the project was announced last week.
before.context: Carbonatite-hosted REE projects commonly rely on airborne magnetics to delineate intrusive boundaries and structural controls ahead of maiden drilling, so this is standard early-stage work. The rapid mobilisation—fieldwork starting within a week of the project announcement—suggests AuKing is pursuing an aggressive timeline at Tundulu.
before.what_to_watch: Survey results (magnetic data and 3D inversions) expected within 7–10 days; watch for refined drill targets and confirmation of May rig mobilisation at Tundulu.
before.key_facts: ["~330 line-km drone magnetics and LiDAR survey completed across the entire 5 km Tundulu carbonatite complex, covering Nathace, Makhanga, Namuka, Ichigwakalu and Tundulu hills","Processed geophysical products—including levelled magnetic data, 3D inversions and derived grids—are expected within 7–10 days","Discussions with a preferred drilling contractor are underway, targeting commencement of maiden drilling in May following community engagement and regulatory approvals"]

before.context: These grades are far above typical Cobar-style base metal deposit norms of 5–10% combined Pb+Zn and rival some of the highest-grade massive sulphide intercepts seen in the Australian polymetallic space. The 10km proximity to Aurelia’s Hera processing plant means near-mine discoveries at Federation can potentially be blended into the mine plan with minimal capital delay.
before.grade_commentary: The 28.3% Zn and 15.4% Pb (39.4% Zn and 21.4% Pb included) over 3.8m ETW is bonanza-grade polymetallic mineralisation — roughly 4–8 times typical Cobar Basin base metal grades and highly economic if continuity holds. The 0.9m drilled width (0.3m ETW) intercept at 158.4 g/t Au is exceptional gold grade but extremely narrow, implying selective mining methods if mined standalone. The Harley Lens intercept of 16.4% Zn and 8.3% Pb over 3.0m ETW and the FDR0395 intercept of 31.8% Zn and 16.5% Pb over 2.8m ETW are also very high-grade and likely amenable to standard underground extraction. Federation West remains open down-dip with a further 150m of potential to the interpreted thrust fault.
before.key_facts: ["FDR0354 returned a bonanza-grade down-dip extension of 9.0m (3.8m ETW) @ 28.3% Zn, 15.4% Pb, 1.2% Cu, 0.9g/t Au and 27g/t Ag, including 5.4m (2.3m ETW) @ 39.4% Zn, 21.4% Pb, 1.7% Cu, 1.4g/t Au and 36g/t Ag — roughly 70m below previously known mineralisation and open at depth.","The same hole FDR0354 produced multiple additional threshold-exceeding intercepts: 1.9m (0.8m ETW) @ 10.6% Zn and 6.3% Pb; 3.9m (1.5m ETW) @ 3.5% Zn, 4.9% Pb and 43.0g/t Au including 0.9m (0.3m ETW) @ 158.4g/t Au; 4.2m (1.6m ETW) @ 5.2% Zn and 3.4% Pb; 1.8m (0.7m ETW) @ 6.6% Zn and 2.7% Pb; and 9.9m (3.7m ETW) @ 14.3% Zn, 6.7% Pb, 0.6% Cu and 0.4g/t Au.","The new Harley Lens was confirmed ~140m northwest of Federation West with intercepts such as 4.0m (3.0m ETW) @ 16.4% Zn, 8.3% Pb and 19g/t Ag, while hole FDR0395 hit 5.5m (2.8m ETW) @ 31.8% Zn, 16.5% Pb within 1.8m of active workings outside the current mine plan."]

before.summary: Auravelle Metals has identified new drill targets at the Bimba and Myall prospects within its Nuckulla Hill Gold Project in South Australia, drawing on historical drilling data and a recent detailed magnetic survey. The targets sit along the Yarlbrinda Shear Zone — which hosts Barton Gold’s neighboring 1.6 Moz Tunkillia project — and are heritage cleared ahead of an upcoming RC and aircore drilling campaign. The announcement contains no new assay results but confirms a pipeline of near-term drill tests.
before.grade_commentary: The 1.1 g/t Au intercepts over 24m and 10m are low-moderate grade — acceptable for bulk open-pit scenarios if continuity and tonnage prove sufficient, but marginal for underground mining. The 1m @ 4.2 g/t Au interval is moderate grade but far too narrow to be economic on its own and would require costly selective mining. None of the reported historical results reach bonanza grade (>10 g/t Au), and economic viability here would hinge on large-scale, consistent mineralisation rather than high-grade shoots.
before.key_facts: ["Bimba and Myall prospects display 500m+ strike lengths of gold anomalism from historical drilling, with broad intercepts of 24m @ 1.1 g/t Au and 10m @ 1.1 g/t Au at Bimba, plus 1m @ 2.2 g/t Au at Myall; both remain open along strike and at depth.","Sheoak, Sheoak East, Bimba and Myall are heritage cleared and scheduled for an upcoming RC infill/extension program, followed by a discovery-focused aircore campaign across the 40km Yarlbrinda Shear Zone.","The targets lie within the Yarlbrinda Shear Zone, which hosts Barton Gold Holdings’ 1.6 Moz Tunkillia Gold Project immediately to the south."]

before.summary: AusQuest has reported results from nine of thirteen RC drill holes at its Cangallo copper-gold project in Peru, outlining a mineralised corridor stretching more than 1,500 metres. The holes returned broad intercepts of 0.25–0.29% copper over hundreds of metres, alongside narrower higher-grade intervals including 12 metres at 1.09% copper and 0.01 g/t gold, suggesting potential for a richer core within the porphyry system. Several holes ended in mineralisation, and a 5,000-metre diamond drilling campaign is scheduled for late May to test for deeper, higher-grade sulphide mineralisation.
before.context: Peruvian porphyry operations in the Arequipa District such as Zafranal and Tia Maria target similar head grades of 0.20–0.40% Cu, making Cangallo's broad intercepts comparable, but the emerging +1% Cu dyke-hosted mineralisation suggests potential for a significantly higher-grade core rare at this shallow level.
before.grade_commentary: For a porphyry copper deposit, the broad 0.25–0.29% Cu intercepts over 184–269m are typical and economically relevant at scale, matching the feed grades of regional Peruvian mines. The narrower intervals grading 0.77–1.09% Cu are exceptional for the deposit type and indicate potential for supergene enrichment or a proximal higher-grade hypogene centre; however, true widths are unknown because the RC drilling is wide spaced and the orientation of the steep dykes has not yet been determined by diamond drilling.
before.key_facts: ["High-grade intercepts exceed typical porphyry norms by more than 2×: CANRC048 returned 12m @ 1.09% Cu and 0.01 g/t Au from 112m, while CANRC047 returned 12m @ 0.77% Cu and 0.08 g/t Au from 102m, both well above the 0.20–0.40% Cu head grades common to producing Peruvian porphyry mines.","CANRC045 contained multiple threshold-exceeding intercepts within a single broad envelope: 269m @ 0.29% Cu and 0.05 g/t Au from 160m to EOH (open at depth), including 38m @ 0.34% Cu, 32m @ 0.44% Cu, 46m @ 0.38% Cu, and 10m @ 0.61% Cu from 276m.","The mineralised corridor now exceeds 1,500m in strike and remains open in multiple directions; four RC holes are pending assays and a 5,000m diamond drill program is slated for late May to target higher-grade copper sulphide extensions at depth."]

before.summary: Austral Resources (AR1) announced exceptional copper intercepts from the first-ever drill hole at its Snow Queen satellite prospect, located 60 km west of the Rocklands Processing Facility. Drillhole 26SQRC001 returned 10 m @ 7.52% Cu from 35 m downhole, including a bonanza-grade 4 m @ 15.98% Cu, within a breccia system at the Hardway Granite–Corella Formation contact. True widths are not yet known, and gold assays are pending.
before.context: The intercepts compare exceptionally against Austral’s existing 64 Mt @ 0.73% Cu resource base and typical Mount Isa district copper grades of 0.5–1.5% Cu. At 15.98% Cu, the included interval represents bonanza-grade mineralisation rarely seen in bulk mining contexts and could represent a high-grade satellite feed source for the company’s hub-and-spoke strategy.
before.what_to_watch: Receipt of full multi-element and gold assays for 26SQRC001 (expected within the week); assay results from follow-up drillhole 26SQRC002 (expected in 2–4 weeks); restart of regional drilling programme in Q3 2026 targeting priority prospects.

before.summary: Australian Rare Earths Ltd (AR3) has commenced uranium drilling at its Overland Project in South Australia, targeting two sedimentary-hosted zones defined by historic 1979–82 drilling. The program follows resampling of historic core hole C051, which returned narrow intercepts up to 201 ppm U3O8, and will test mineralisation continuity and thickness. The company says its balance sheet remains strong, allowing concurrent advancement of the Koppamurra Rare Earths Project Pre-Feasibility Study.
before.context: South Australia is a premier uranium jurisdiction, but the historic intercepts of ~150–200 ppm U3O8 (0.015–0.02% U3O8) sit well below typical economic thresholds for most uranium deposits (commonly >500–1,000 ppm or >0.05% U3O8), meaning the investment case hinges on finding thicker, higher-grade extensions rather than these narrow historic hits.
before.grade_commentary: The historic intercepts of 153–201 ppm U3O8 are very low grade by uranium industry standards and would be considered sub-economic in isolation. Combined with narrow widths of 0.44–0.90m, these results alone do not outline a viable deposit. The exploration thesis rests on the potential for broader, higher-grade zones within the sedimentary targets.
before.key_facts: ["Historic drillhole C051 returned three intercepts interpreted as true widths: 0.44m @ 159 ppm U3O8 from 56.6m, 0.70m @ 153 ppm U3O8 from 57.3m, and 0.90m @ 201 ppm U3O8 from 60.3m — all from shallow depths above a brown coal deposit.","The new drilling targets two sedimentary-hosted uranium zones (Western Flank and Basal Sandy Unit) in the Murray Basin; the Western Flank remains largely open toward the regional Palmer Fault.","The company describes its balance sheet as 'strong' but provides no specific cash, debt or shares-outstanding figures in this release."]

before.grade_commentary: For an ionic clay REE deposit, 1,013ppm TREO is a moderate baseline resource grade; intercepts of 3,055–8,517ppm TREO represent exceptional to bonanza grades within the system. The thick intervals (6–13m) starting from as shallow as 1m depth are highly favourable for ISR wellfield economics, as they minimise installation depth and maximise recovery potential. Because mineralisation is flat-lying and all holes are vertical, reported downhole widths approximate true widths.
before.key_facts: ["Standout intercept CLD-AUG-682 hit 1m @ 8,517ppm TREO (41% MREO) and 10m @ 3,055ppm TREO — roughly 8.4 times the Woolrich deposit's 1,013ppm Inferred resource grade.","Four separate holes delivered multiple >2x-resource-grade intercepts in a single hole: CLD-AUG-652 (4m @ 3,740ppm and 1m @ 7,331ppm TREO), CLD-AUG-682 (10m @ 3,055ppm and 1m @ 8,517ppm TREO), CLD-AUG-673 (3m @ 3,736ppm and 1m @ 5,340ppm TREO), and CLD-AUG-696 (4m @ 3,540ppm and 1m @ 7,475ppm TREO).","Results confirm a high-value HREE enrichment signature (Dy, Tb, Y), differentiating Woolrich from typical Brazilian LREE deposits and aligning it with higher-value southern Chinese ionic clay analogues."]

before.summary: Barton Gold reported reverse circulation drill assays from the Challenger West open pit floor, returning bonanza grades up to 59.5 g/t Au over 1 metre within a broader 3-metre interval at 20.6 g/t Au. The shallow intersections (0–28 metres) confirm near-surface, high-value mineralisation that could be excavated to supplement feed for a Stage 1 restart of the nearby Central Gawler Mill. The results will feed a JORC resource upgrade and ongoing DFS, with further assays pending along strike.
before.context: These intercepts significantly exceed the Challenger resource grade of 0.92 g/t Au and align with the historic high-grade, narrow-vein style of the 2002–2018 Challenger mine. The shallow, excavatable depth (<30 m) suits a low-cost, low-risk Stage 1 mill-restart feed strategy without disturbing deeper underground infrastructure.
before.what_to_watch: Assays from the Challenger South-Southwest and Challenger 3 targets — drilled along strike from Main and West — are expected within 4–8 weeks and could expand the near-surface mineable inventory. Investors should also watch for the DFS progress on the Stage 1 baseline operation and any resulting JORC resource upgrade to Indicated category.
before.key_facts: ["CHB0150 returned 3m @ 20.6 g/t Au including 1m @ 59.5 g/t Au from 13 metres depth — bonanza grade roughly 65× the Challenger resource grade of 0.92 g/t Au.","CHB0149 returned 7m @ 2.01 g/t Au from surface including 1m @ 9.63 g/t Au from 6 metres, confirming near-surface continuity in the pit floor.","Assays are pending for the Challenger South-Southwest and Challenger 3 targets drilled along strike, with results expected in the next 4–8 weeks."]

before.summary: Barton Gold reported new RC drill assays from the Challenger South-Southwest (CSSW) and Challenger 3 targets at its Challenger Gold Project in South Australia. The results confirm near-surface, open-pittable mineralisation with multiple intercepts grading 1.3–4.5 g/t Au over 6–10m and including narrower high-grade zones up to 16.5 g/t Au. The company says the results support a potential maiden JORC Mineral Resource Estimate at Challenger 3 and could provide low-risk mill feed for the planned Stage 1 restart of the Central Gawler Mill.
before.grade_commentary: The reported intercepts include high-grade zones up to 16.5 g/t Au and 12.1 g/t Au over 1–2m, which are exceptional compared to the Challenger resource grade of 0.92 g/t Au. Broader intervals of 6–10m at 1.3–4.5 g/t Au are also well above the deposit average and attractive for open-pit bulk mining. All widths are downhole lengths; true widths are variable and generally narrower due to steeply dipping lode orientations.
before.key_facts: ["CHB0222 returned 7m @ 3.28 g/t Au from 30m including 1m @ 16.5 g/t Au, and CHB0204 returned 6m @ 4.46 g/t Au from 30m including 2m @ 12.1 g/t Au — grades far exceeding the Challenger resource average of 0.92 g/t Au","CHB0198 contained multiple threshold-exceeding intercepts in one hole: 3m @ 2.38 g/t Au, 3m @ 3.17 g/t Au, and 1m @ 2.05 g/t Au, all more than double the existing resource grade","Results support a maiden JORC (2012) Mineral Resource Estimate at the Challenger 3 target and remain open to extension along strike and at depth"]

before.context: Tunkillia’s starter-pit economics and sub-one-year payback are standout metrics for a pre-production gold developer, contrasting with typical Australian open-pit projects that often target 3–5 year paybacks; the project also benefits from Barton’s 100%-owned, fully permitted Central Gawler Mill at Challenger, providing near-term infrastructure optionality that most peers lack.
before.grade_commentary: The Phase 1 intercepts of 2–5 g/t Au over 10–47m are well above Tunkillia’s 0.87 g/t Au average resource grade and are highly encouraging for a bulk open-pit operation. Narrow 1m–2m inclusions above 20 g/t Au, including a peak of 43.2 g/t Au, are bonanza grades but likely represent discrete high-grade shoots; without reported estimated true widths, these should be viewed as apparent widths. The broader, lower-grade envelopes are the key economic driver, as they are amenable to bulk mining and align with the 'Starter Pit' concept that underpins the project’s rapid payback.

before.summary: Avira Resources has secured the key regulatory, environmental and heritage approvals needed to start a 4,500-metre RC drill program at its Mt Cattlin Gold Project in Western Australia. The approvals cover four prospects including the historically high-grade Sirdar and Maori Queen deposits, with on-ground activities set to commence once the final heritage notice is received. The company is targeting a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate in Q3–Q4 2026 following the drill program.
before.context: The 24.56 g/t Au historical grade places Mt Cattlin well above typical Yilgarn underground mines (often 2–5 g/t Au resource grade) and in line with other narrow-vein high-grade camps, though the small historical tonnage suggests mineralisation is locally concentrated. The project sits in the Ravensthorpe Greenstone Belt near Medallion Metals' 1.3Moz Kundip Gold Project and adjacent to Rio Tinto's Mt Cattlin lithium mine, providing district-scale geological validation.
before.what_to_watch: Receipt of the WKSNAC Preliminary Advice Notice — the final statutory trigger for on-ground activities — followed by commencement of RC drilling at Maori Queen and Sirdar in Q2 2026 and assay results from the program.

before.grade_commentary: The reported tungsten intercepts — notably 26m at 0.24% WO₃ and internal zones up to 0.9% WO₃ — are moderate-to-high grade for a by-product credit in an orogenic gold system. Standalone tungsten operations often require >0.2% WO₃, so the broader 0.09–0.11% WO₃ intervals would rely on the high-grade gold offsets and coarse-grained, gravity-recoverable nature of the scheelite/ferberite to contribute value. No estimated true widths are reported; all intercepts are downhole lengths. The company does not state whether tungsten mineralisation remains open at depth or along strike.

before.summary: Benz Mining has confirmed widespread tungsten mineralisation across the 12km Glenburgh gold corridor in Western Australia through lithium borate fusion re-assays of existing RC drill holes. Three holes returned significant tungsten intercepts — including 26m at 0.24% WO3 and internal intervals up to 0.9% WO3 — with mineralogy confirming coarse-grained scheelite and ferberite potentially amenable to simple gravity recovery. The results suggest tungsten could provide a by-product credit to the gold system, though true widths remain unmodelled and formal metallurgical testwork is only just underway.
before.key_facts: ["Standout high-grade internal intervals include 11m at 0.55% WO3 within 25GLR_023, 2m at 0.57% and 4m at 0.42% WO3 within 26HZ002, and 1m at 0.9% WO3 within 25GLR_070 — well above typical by-product grades in bulk-tonnage gold systems.","Hole 26HZ002 returned multiple threshold-exceeding intercepts: 33m at 0.10% WO3 (including 2m at 0.57% and 4m at 0.42% WO3), plus 10m at 0.01% WO3 and 10m at 0.03% WO3.","Hole 25GLR_023 also returned multiple intercepts: 26m at 0.24% WO3 (including 11m at 0.55%), 5m at 0.11% WO3, and additional lower-grade zones — all reported as downhole lengths with true widths pending geological modelling."]

before.summary: BPM Minerals has completed heritage surveys, airborne magnetics, and roughly 1,500 soil samples at the Bonnie & Clyde prospect on its Forelands Gold Project in WA, with assays expected in four to six weeks. The company remains on track for maiden RC drilling in Q3 2026 after securing WA government co-funding for a future IP survey and advancing its Program of Work application. Historical intercepts at the nearby Beachcomber prospect—including 3m @ 65.8 g/t Au and multiple hits in hole FLRC010—are cited as evidence of the project's high-grade potential.
before.context: The Forelands Project sits on the Yilgarn–Albany Fraser margin, the same tectonic setting as the +8 Moz Tropicana gold deposit, and is located roughly 150 km east of Kalgoorlie with access to multiple regional mills.
before.key_facts: ["Bonnie & Clyde soil anomaly returned individual values >1 g/t Au (1,000,000 ppb) within a coherent >100 ppb Au envelope across an untested ~6 km strike—exceptionally anomalous for surface geochemistry.","Historical Beachcomber drilling includes multiple bonanza-grade intercepts in a single hole: FLRC010 returned 6m @ 6.72 g/t Au from 28m and 2m @ 20.77 g/t Au from 40m.","Maiden RC drilling at Bonnie & Clyde remains targeted for Q3 2026, contingent on receipt of a Program of Work from the WA Department of Mines in the coming months."]

before.summary: BCM released an investor presentation for RIU Sydney reiterating its Ema ionic clay rare earths project, highlighting a 1,071 Mt resource, US$55M pre-production CAPEX, and US$8–10/kg TREO operating costs via in-situ recovery. The company confirmed it is not aware of any new material information and outlined a path toward a Bankable Feasibility Study in Q2 2026, offtake discussions in Q2, and project financing in Q3. The deck emphasizes the project's high magnet rare earth content (~41% MREO:TREO) and low-cost scalability versus larger Brazilian peers.
before.grade_commentary: The in-situ resource grade of ~732 ppm TREO is typical for ionic clay rare earth deposits, but the ~41–42% MREO:TREO ratio is notably high, supporting a basket price of roughly US$54/kg (NdPrDyTb basis). Field trial leaching achieved TREO grades up to 7,800 ppm and MREO above 3,500 ppm, indicating strong metallurgical extraction potential, though full-scale commercial recoveries remain to be demonstrated in the BFS.

before.grade_commentary: The reported results of up to 71 ppb Au (0.071 g/t Au) are geochemically anomalous but sub-economic by several orders of magnitude. Economic gold deposits typically require bedrock grades >0.3 g/t Au for bulk mining and >2–3 g/t Au for narrow vein deposits. These trace values in transported lacustrine sediments and saprolite represent a possible dispersion halo from weathered basement sources, not mineable mineralisation, and cannot support a resource estimate.

before.summary: Burley Minerals published a strategic and exploration update on its 100% owned Chubb Lithium Project near Val d’Or, Quebec, reiterating historical drill intercepts up to 1.7% Li₂O and rare pollucite (caesium) results alongside previously reported metallurgical testwork showing >6% Li₂O concentrate grades at 60–72% recovery. Citing improved lithium prices, the company disclosed it is actively reviewing whether to advance exploration, seek a joint venture partner, or sell the asset. The project lies just 15 km from Canada’s only producing lithium mine (North American Lithium) and only 6 of its 35 claims have been drill-tested to date.
before.grade_commentary: For hard-rock spodumene pegmatites, intercepts of 1.5–1.7% Li₂O over 3–9m drilled width are moderate-to-high grade and sit above the 1.0–1.15% Li₂O typical of nearby projects like NAL and Authier. However, estimated true widths are not disclosed, so economic thickness remains unconfirmed. The pollucite grades (up to 6.8% Cs₂O over 2.8m) are exceptional by global standards given the scarcity of economic caesium deposits.
before.key_facts: ["Multiple historical holes returned stacked pegmatite intercepts: CLP066 hit 3.0m at 1.7% Li₂O and 3.6m at 1.0% Li₂O; CLP065 hit 6.1m at 1.2% Li₂O and 6.1m at 1.0% Li₂O; CLP043 hit 3.9m at 1.5% Li₂O and 4.5m at 1.0% Li₂O.","Rare pollucite (caesium) intersections include 6.8% Cs₂O over 2.8m in CLP-038 and 2.4% Cs₂O over 4.0m (including 2.0m at 4.2% Cs₂O) in CLP-063 — pollucite is a critical mineral with virtually no current mine supply.","Burley launched a strategic review of Chubb to evaluate further exploration, joint venture, or sale; the project is 15 km from Canada’s only producing lithium mine (North American Lithium) and 85% of claims remain untested by drilling."]

before.grade_commentary: These historical intercepts represent bonanza-grade polymetallic mineralization. before.summary: Caprice Resources reported exceptional shallow drill results from its Island Gold Project, with RC hole 26IGRC010 intersecting 22 metres at 66.2 g/t gold—including 8 metres at 181 g/t and 2 metres at 686 g/t—from just 42 metres downhole in a new lode ~120m west of the main Vadrians deposit. The result validates the model that high-grade mineralisation exists beneath weathered depletion zones and significantly expands the project's multi-lode potential, with follow-up drilling already underway.
before.context: These intercepts far exceed typical Murchison greenstone gold grades of 1–3 g/t Au and are comparable to high-grade discovery holes seen in tier-one WA orogenic camps. The shallow depth and interpreted 60–70% true width suggest stronger geometry than typical narrow vein systems, enhancing the project's potential scale.
before.grade_commentary: 66.2 g/t Au over 22m is bonanza-grade and exceptional for an orogenic gold system; with an estimated true width of 60–70% (roughly 13–15 metres), this is a thick, high-value intercept. The included 8m at 181 g/t Au is also remarkable, while the 2m at 686 g/t Au, though spectacular, represents a narrower internal high. The shallow start depth of 42m materially enhances the potential economic relevance if continuity is confirmed.
before.key_facts: ["RC hole 26IGRC010 returned 22m @ 66.2 g/t Au (ETW est. ~13–15m) including 8m @ 181 g/t Au and 2m @ 686 g/t Au from 42m downhole in a new high-grade lode ~120m west of Vadrians.","The same hole also intersected 9m @ 2.81 g/t Au including 5m @ 4.52 g/t Au from 186m in the Vadrians BIF, confirming two significant intercepts in one hole.","Follow-up RC drilling is planned to recommence next week beneath the bonanza intercept, with three diamond holes also pending assays testing depth extensions at Vadrians."]

before.summary: Carnavale Resources has published an updated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Kookynie Gold Project in Western Australia, with total resources now at 855,000 tonnes grading 4.4 g/t gold for 120,000 ounces. A major upgrade in confidence sees 182,000 tonnes at 5.1 g/t Au classified as Measured — representing 58% of the shallow open-pit material above the 320mRL — which significantly de-risks the upcoming Bankable Feasibility Study. The bonanza-grade core remains open at depth and the BFS is expected in Q3 2026.
before.grade_commentary: The global resource grade of 4.4 g/t Au is high for an open-pit development, with the shallow open-pit component averaging 3.9 g/t Au and the underground component averaging 4.8 g/t Au. The bonanza shoots grading >29 g/t Au are exceptional, though the narrow 2–3m vein thickness implies selective mining may be needed to realise that value. Metallurgical recoveries of 97–99% are excellent.

before.summary: Centaurus Metals published its 2025 Sustainability Report, providing a consolidated update on the Jaguar Nickel Sulphide Project (JNP). The report highlights the receipt of final key Brazilian regulatory approvals—the Installation Licence in March 2025 and Mining Lease in October 2025—a binding offtake with Glencore for roughly one-third of forecast output, and JVEP economics showing first-quartile C1 cash costs of US$3.34/lb Ni and a 34% IRR. The company targets a Final Investment Decision in the second half of 2026 and first production in 2029, backed by 100% renewable power and a carbon footprint roughly 86% below the industry average.
before.verdict_reason: The filing compiles multiple major de-risking milestones for Jaguar—key approvals, Glencore offtake, and reaffirmed first-quartile project economics—that underpin the pathway to a targeted H2 2026 Final Investment Decision, even if largely previously announced.

before.summary: Catalina Resources has received all assays from its 8,452m RC program across the Central Yilgarn projects, defining a continuous 12–14 km gold corridor now named the Palisade Gold Project. The standout result remains a near-surface 48m @ 2.61 g/t Au intersection at Chicken Little (open at depth), while new Snowflake assays extended mineralisation roughly 50 m along strike and the company outlined conceptual Exploration Targets of 60,000–330,000 oz Au.
before.context: The shallow, high-grade Chicken Little intercept is comparable to early-stage Yilgarn greenstone discoveries that have advanced to open-pit resources, though true widths remain unconfirmed. The conceptual 60,000–330,000 oz Exploration Target is modest by ASX junior standards and requires substantial infill drilling to be upgraded to a JORC Mineral Resource.
before.grade_commentary: The 48m @ 2.61 g/t Au intersection at Chicken Little is excellent for a shallow open-pit target, with internal zones above 5 g/t Au reaching bonanza grades; the 1–2m Snowflake intersections around 1.6–1.7 g/t Au are moderate but attractive given their shallow depth. However, true widths are currently unknown, and the narrow 1m zones at Snowflake may represent selective mining targets rather than bulk-tonnage envelopes if true widths are similarly constrained. The broader T8 intersections (0.59–1.38 g/t Au) are moderate and deeper, consistent with a structurally controlled system.
before.key_facts: ["Standout near-surface intercept at Chicken Little of 48m @ 2.61 g/t Au from 15m (open at depth), including internal high-grade zones of 20m @ 5.64 g/t Au and 8m @ 11.6 g/t Au — well above typical open-pit grade norms.","Hole 26YGRC022 at Chicken Little returned multiple mineralised intervals: 48m @ 2.61 g/t Au, 3m @ 1.12 g/t Au, and 3m @ 0.96 g/t Au, with internal zones grading up to 16 g/t Au over 1m.","New Snowflake assays extended mineralisation ~50 m north and south of historical drilling, returning shallow intersections including 2m @ 1.70 g/t Au and 1m @ 1.67 g/t Au, with the system open along strike."]

before.grade_commentary: TREO grades of ~1,400–1,550 ppm (0.14–0.15%) from surface are moderate-to-high for ionic adsorption clay (IAC) REE deposits, broadly in line with economic thresholds seen in comparable Brazilian and Chinese clay-hosted projects. The 380% grade upgrade in fine clay fraction versus bulk samples is the most significant finding, indicating traditional bulk sampling significantly under-reported true REE content. True width is unknown; all auger holes are vertical and most ended prematurely in quartz rubble, leaving mineralisation open at depth.
before.key_facts: ["Fine fraction sieved samples returned grades up to 380% higher than bulk samples, with ITTR001 hitting 1,646ppm TREO in the top metre — confirming REE are preferentially concentrated in clays and that bulk sampling under-reports true grade.","ITTR001 returned multiple high-grade intercepts in the fine fraction: 0-1m @ 1,646ppm TREO and 3-4m @ 1,523ppm TREO, with all six consecutive metre samples from surface grading >1,270ppm TREO.","The project was acquired from Rio Tinto in December 2025 and these first-pass auger results validate historical soil anomalies, yet approximately 90% of the 317km² tenement area remains unexplored."]

The 380% grade upgrade in fine clay fraction versus bulk samples is the most significant finding, indicating traditional bulk sampling significantly under-reported true REE content. True width is unknown; all auger holes are vertical and most ended prematurely in quartz rubble, leaving mineralisation open at depth.

before.summary: Corazon Mining’s maiden diamond drill program at the Two Pools Gold Project in Western Australia’s Plutonic-Marymia belt intersected gold mineralisation in all four holes, with the best result of 2.0m @ 1.50 g/t Au (incl. 0.5m @ 4.59 g/t Au) in TPDD0002. Core logging has revised the interpreted vein orientation from northwest to east-west, providing a clearer structural model to guide an upcoming follow-up RC program targeting extensions open at depth and along strike. The company also secured Exploration Licence E52/4521 and intersected a substantial pegmatite dyke (~25–40m thick, >500m strike) that remains open in all directions.
before.grade_commentary: The best intercept of 4.59 g/t Au over 0.5m is high-grade but very narrow, likely representing a thin quartz vein that would require selective mining; most other intercepts (0.5–0.8 g/t Au over 0.4–2.0m) are low to moderate by Yilgarn orogenic standards and are more typical of shear-hosted disseminated targets. All widths are reported as drilled widths; true widths have not been calculated and could be narrower.
before.key_facts: ["TPDD0002 returned multiple gold intercepts: 2.0m @ 1.50 g/t Au (incl. 0.5m @ 4.59 g/t Au) and 1.59m @ 0.60 g/t Au (incl. 0.5m @ 1.54 g/t Au).","Diamond core logging revised the interpreted gold-bearing vein orientation from northwest to east-west, directly informing the design of follow-up RC drill holes to target down-dip and along-strike extensions.","A substantial pegmatite dyke (~25–40m thick, traced over >500m of strike) was intersected and remains open in all directions, interpreted as a potential fluid-focusing structure with additional mineral potential."]

before.summary: Dreadnought Resources has reported exceptional extensional RC drill results from Metzke's Find at its Illaara Gold Project in Western Australia, highlighted by 7m @ 49.9 g/t Au — the highest-grade intercept recorded to date. All 23 reported holes intersected the shear lode horizon and the new results sit entirely outside the existing 2023 high-grade resource of 14,900 oz @ 6.8 g/t Au, confirming mineralisation remains open along strike and at depth. The company expects final assays in June 2026 ahead of an upgraded resource and initial scoping study in July 2026.
before.ticker_summary: DRE hits 49.9 g/t Au over 7m at Metzke's Find — highest grades yet, outside 2023 resource. Resource update due July.
before.context: The 49.9 g/t Au result is bonanza-grade and compares favourably to the historical production grade of ~40 g/t Au from Metzke's Find's early 1900s workings, while far exceeding typical Yilgarn open-pit and underground feed grades. The shallow, free-milling nature of the mineralisation — with combined gravity and CIL recoveries averaging 98.9% — reinforces its potential as a near-term, high-margin development opportunity.
before.grade_commentary: 49.9 g/t Au over 7m is bonanza-grade and more than 7x the existing 6.8 g/t Au resource grade; even at an estimated true width of 70–90% of downhole length, this represents an exceptional intercept for a shear-lode gold system. 23.5 g/t Au over 5m is similarly high-grade. Both intercepts start from just 67m depth, and the coarse-grained, free-milling nature of the gold (98.9% combined recovery) significantly enhances commercial potential.
before.key_facts: ["MZRC123 intersected 7m @ 49.9 g/t Au from 67m — more than 7x the 2023 resource grade of 6.8 g/t Au and the highest-grade intercept yet at Metzke's Find.","MZRC119 returned 5m @ 23.5 g/t Au from 67m, also well above deposit norms and outside the current resource.","All new intercepts sit outside the 2023 high-grade resource (14,900 oz @ 6.8 g/t Au, 72% Indicated), with mineralisation remaining open along strike and at depth; a resource upgrade and scoping study are expected in July 2026."]

before.context: The antimony grades reported—particularly historical sorted ore of 39–76% Sb and recent rock chips of 18–22% Sb—are exceptionally high compared to typical antimony deposits, where >1–2% Sb is generally considered high grade. Taylor represents a rare Nevada district with both past-producing antimony mines and a significant gold-silver system, aligning with renewed U.S. critical mineral interest.
before.grade_commentary: For antimony, grades above 1–2% Sb are typically considered high grade; the historical Merrimac intercepts of 3.3% to 7.0% Sb over 4–12 metre widths starting near surface are strongly mineralized, while the reported historical sorted ore of 39–76% Sb is extraordinary and likely represents hand-sorted stibnite rather than in-situ bulk grade. For gold, 1.02 g/t Au over 18.3m is low-moderate but reasonable for bulk open-pit heap leach scenarios, whereas channel samples of up to 7.1 g/t Au over 3.3m are high grade. True widths were not disclosed for the historical intercepts.

before.summary: Aben Gold Corp. has outlined its fully contracted 2026 exploration program at the Justin Gold Tungsten Project in Yukon, featuring 1,500 metres of diamond drilling across the POW gold-tungsten zone and the high-grade Lost Ace gold zone. Field work is scheduled from mid-July to mid-September 2026, with results expected this fall. Historical intercepts cited include bonanza-grade 88.2 g/t Au over 1.0 metre at Lost Ace and broad intervals of 1.25–1.49 g/t Au at POW.
before.grade_commentary: The Lost Ace channel sample of 88.2 g/t Au over 1.0 m represents bonanza-grade mineralization exceptional for any deposit type, though as a narrow channel sample it requires confirmation by diamond drilling. At POW, the broad intervals of 1.25–1.49 g/t Au over 46–60 metres are moderate-grade, typical of intrusion-related gold systems amenable to bulk mining, while the 8.20 g/t Au over 2.60 m sub-interval is high-grade. The tungsten intercept of 1.12% WO₃ over 1.0 m is a moderate-grade critical mineral occurrence.

before.context: Saskatchewan potash deposits typically average 20–25% KCl; Disley’s ~35% KCl grade is exceptionally high and supports strong project economics. before.grade_commentary: A KCl grade of ~35% is excellent for a Saskatchewan potash deposit and sits well above the 20–25% typical of conventional sylvinite operations. before.summary: AbraSilver has finalized the acquisition of the Condoryacu and Maria Amalia properties adjacent to its Diablillos project in Argentina, paying US$2.75 million total. Initial confirmatory drilling at Condoryacu returned a standout 72-metre intercept grading 18.7 g/t gold, 117 g/t silver and 2.06% copper from surface — the strongest gold grade-thickness ever reported in the district — while Oculto East saw a broad 207.5-metre oxide intercept. The results suggest a significant, high-grade sulphide system adjacent to the existing oxide resource, with follow-up drilling already underway and DFS completion targeted for Q2/2026.
before.grade_commentary: 18.74 g/t Au is bonanza grade and the 72 m drilled width is remarkable even before true width is calculated; this far exceeds the Diablillos resource average of 0.51 g/t Au and even the 0.66 g/t Au tank-leach grade. The multiple stacked intercepts in DDH 26-003 — including 11.86 g/t Au over 5.0 m and 5.24 g/t Au over 12.0 m — confirm a robust sulphide system from surface, though true widths are unknown and selective mining may be required if veins narrow. The 207.5 m of 0.48 g/t Au at Oculto East is low-moderate grade but consistent with bulk-tonnage oxide open-pit feed.
before.key_facts: ["DDH 26-002 at Condoryacu returned 72.0 m of 18.74 g/t Au, 117.4 g/t Ag and 2.06% Cu from surface (0 m downhole) — the strongest gold grade-thickness intersection ever reported in the Diablillos district.","DDH 26-003 intersected four stacked high-grade sulphide zones: 5.0 m of 11.86 g/t Au, 18.0 m of 4.11 g/t Au, 2.0 m of 1.21 g/t Au, and 12.0 m of 5.24 g/t Au, all with associated silver and copper values.","AbraSilver completed the Condoryacu and Maria Amalia acquisitions with final cash payments of US$2.5 million and US$250,000, respectively, consolidating land immediately adjacent to Diablillos."]

While the historical grades are eye-catching, they come from a small oxidized-cap shipment and the deeper sulphide-rich CRD core — typically the most productive part of these systems — remains completely untested by modern exploration.

before.context: The ~35% KCl grade sits at the high end of Saskatchewan’s Prairie Evaporite formation, where typical sylvinite resources often grade 20–30% KCl; the HLD method differentiates the project from conventional underground potash mines by using patented horizontal wells to selectively dissolve high-grade potash seams, analogous in concept to horizontal drilling in oil and gas but applied to solution mining.
before.grade_commentary: A KCl grade of ~35% (equivalent to ~22% K2O) is considered high-grade for Saskatchewan potash and well above typical commercial thresholds of 15–25% K2O in the Prairie Evaporite. The HLD selective solution mining approach is designed to target thin high-grade seams within an approximate 0.9m mining cut, leaving lower-grade halite in place; while this improves head grade, it demands precise wellbore placement and brine chemistry control to manage dissolution rates and avoid unwanted carnallite or insoluble buildup.
before.key_facts: ["The April 15, 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate reports 399.7 Mt Measured and 1,267.4 Mt Indicated at an average grade of ~34.8% KCl (22.0% K2O), plus 2,663.2 Mt Inferred at ~35.0% KCl — a tier-one scale potash inventory in Saskatchewan.","Combined project after-tax economics at an 8% discount rate yield an NPV of $1,085M, an IRR of 30%, and a 4.7-year payback from IPM startup; the standalone IPM phase shows an NPV of $195M with ~12-month payback and 104% IRR.","The proposed Horizontal Line-Drive selective solution mining method targets only high-grade seams within a 0.9m mining cut, with an initial 125,000 t/a IPM module planned to confirm and optimize recovery before constructing the two 500,000 t/a HLD mines."]

before.summary: Aeris Resources reported exceptional underground drill results from its Tritton Operation in NSW. At Avoca Tank, a new high-grade copper trend now connects to the central corridor with hits up to 8.48% Cu over 9.5m ETW, while mineralisation has been traced over more than 160m of strike — double the historical length. At Budgerygar, thick intersections up to 39.5m at 1.72% Cu support upgrading the current Inferred Resource to Indicated status.
before.context: These intercepts compare favourably to typical Australian underground copper mines, where feed grades often average 1–2% Cu. Near-mine extensions that lift both tonnage and grade are highly accretive for an operating producer like Aeris because they leverage existing mill and underground infrastructure with minimal incremental capital.
before.what_to_watch: Monitor the Q4 FY26 Mineral Resource update for both Avoca Tank and Budgerygar, plus pending assays from holes ATEL156–158 and upcoming results from the Tritton Deeps extension program.

before.context: The N2 Project sits in the Abitibi greenstone belt near the Casa Berardi trend, where bulk-tonnage deposits typically run 1–2 g/t Au; the recent wide, near-surface intercepts align with open-pit potential, while the narrower high-grade RJ Zone resembles the nearby former Vezza underground mine. At current gold prices, a 1.4 g/t Au bulk deposit in this jurisdiction attracts renewed interest, but the historical resource requires modern verification drilling before it can be treated as current.
before.grade_commentary: The recent intercepts are mostly low-to-moderate grade (0.95–1.8 g/t Au) over wide widths (21–61 metres), consistent with bulk-tonnage, open-pit targets in the Abitibi. The 19.2 g/t Au over 0.51 metres in N2-25-012 is bonanza grade but extremely narrow, implying selective mining rather than bulk feed, while the 3.51 g/t Au over 10.5 metres is a genuine high-grade interval for this deposit type. None of the reported intercepts yet approach the RJ Zone’s historic average of 7.82 g/t Au, which remains the project’s high-grade outlier.

before.summary: Aguia Resources reported that its Santa Barbara narrow-vein gold mine in Colombia achieved a significant jump in estimated head grades to 12 g/t Au (10.31 g/t Au recovered) in the final April batch, roughly triple the prior 3–4 g/t Au average, after optimizing mining methods and tightening grade control. Total April production was only 80 tonnes of ore because crews focused on sinking two shafts beneath Vein #1 and advancing raises on Vein #2 rather than extracting from stopes. The company also confirmed that no JORC Mineral Resource Estimate exists for any of its Colombian projects.
before.grade_commentary: The reported 12 g/t Au head grade (10.31 g/t Au recovered) is bonanza-grade territory for any underground gold deposit and well above typical narrow-vein thresholds. However, this comes from a single small batch during a month with just 80 tonnes total output, and the vein system requires selective mining with true widths estimated at 60–70% of sampled thickness, which limits scalability until wider zones are proven.
before.key_facts: ["Final April batch achieved an estimated head grade of 12 g/t Au (10.31 g/t Au recovered), roughly 3× the prior 3–4 g/t Au nine-month average, following optimized narrow-vein mining methods and tighter dilution control.","Only 80 tonnes of ore were produced in April, with work focused on mine development (two shafts sunk beneath Vein #1, raises on Vein #2); the near-surface upper Stope 1 was permanently abandoned due to strong oxidation and weathering.","The company explicitly states there are no Mineral Resource Estimates on any of its Colombian projects, and true thickness of mineralized intervals is interpreted at 60–70% of sampled thickness."]

before.summary: Alaros Exploration Inc. has filed an NI 43-101 technical report for its newly optioned Birk Creek property in southern British Columbia, confirming a geologic setting analogous to the nearby Yellowhead and Samatosum VMS deposits but establishing no mineral resource. The report compiles historic exploration—including 48 drill holes with base-metal intercepts such as 6.85 m of 2.14% Zn, 0.61% Cu and 16.9 ppm Ag—and recommends a $455,000 two-phase exploration program beginning with data compilation and geophysics. The property remains early-stage, with Alaros required to spend $2.525 million over six years to earn a 100% interest.
before.context: The Birk Creek Property lies within the same Eagle Bay Assemblage that hosts Taseko's Yellowhead copper project—20 km away—with an 817 Mt reserve grading 0.28% Cu, and the past-producing Samatosum mine, demonstrating regional potential for Kuroko-style VMS mineralization. However, the property's shallow-dipping sulphide horizons and extensive overburden make modern geophysical targeting challenging.
before.grade_commentary: Historic trench grades such as 12% Zn and 5.27% Pb are high by VMS standards and exceed the average production grades at the nearby Samatosum mine (1.7% Zn, 0.9% Pb), but the narrow widths (0.4–2.0 m) and lack of true-width confirmation limit near-term economic significance. Drill intercepts such as 6.85 m of 2.14% Zn and 0.61% Cu are moderate-grade, open-pit-style VMS results that would require much wider zones and sustained base-metal prices to support a standalone operation.
before.key_facts: ["Historic trenching returned exceptional base-metal grades well above nearby VMS norms, including 12% Zn over 0.4 m at the Carb showing and 5.27% Pb, 4.15% Zn over 2 m at the Uke showing—multiples higher than the average grades at the past-producing Samatosum mine.","Mineralization was intersected in 46 of 48 historic drill holes across seven northwest-trending horizons, demonstrating widespread VMS potential, yet no mineral resource has been calculated and most historic data predates GPS accuracy.","Alaros optioned the 2,786 ha property in September 2024 for staged payments totaling $825,000 cash and 1.35 million shares, subject to a $2.525 million exploration expenditure commitment over six years and a 3% NSR."]

before.summary: Buffalo Potash Corp. has published an NI 43-101 Preliminary Economic Assessment for its Disley potash project in Saskatchewan, outlining a staged development beginning with a 125,000 tonne-per-year Initial Production Module and expanding to two 500,000 tonne-per-year HLD solution mines. The study reports a combined after-tax NPV8% of $1.085 billion and a 30% IRR, underpinned by a massive 1.67 billion tonne Measured & Indicated resource grading roughly 35% KCl — among the highest grades in the Saskatchewan potash basin. The project uses a patented Horizontal Line-Drive selective solution mining method that targets only high-grade seams, though the 70% mine modification factor still needs confirmation during the pilot phase.
before.context: The grade and scale compare favorably with conventional Saskatchewan potash deposits, which typically mine lower-grade sylvinite at 20–25% KCl; the project’s economics rely on a patented selective solution mining technology rather than traditional shaft mining, placing it closer in risk profile to other innovative potash developers.
before.grade_commentary: ~35% KCl is considered high-grade for Saskatchewan potash; typical Prairie Evaporite sylvinite operations mine grades of roughly 20–25% KCl. The elevated grade supports the selective HLD solution mining thesis, though the mine modification factor of 70% (accounting for anomaly deductions and process losses) still needs confirmation during the IPM phase.
before.key_facts: ["Combined after-tax NPV8% of $1.085 billion and 30% IRR; the IPM phase alone shows $195M NPV and 104% IRR with payback in slightly over 12 months.","Total Measured & Indicated resource of 1,667.1 Mt grading 34.84% KCl (22.0% K2O), with an additional 2,663.2 Mt Inferred — a tier-one scale greenfield potash endowment.","Ore grade of ~35% KCl is significantly above the 20–25% KCl typical of conventional Saskatchewan underground potash operations, supporting the selective HLD mining thesis."]

before.context: The N2 Project’s 1.4–1.5 g/t Au bulk-tonnage historic profile is comparable to other Abitibi open-pit development stories such as Douay, while the 7.82 g/t Au RJ Zone resembles the higher-grade, narrow-vein style of the nearby past-producing Vezza mine. The upsized, flow-through-heavy $22.4 million financing is well above typical CSE explorer raises and removes near-term funding risk.
before.grade_commentary: Near-surface intercepts of 0.95–1.8 g/t Au across 21–61 metres are moderate and consistent with bulk-tonnage open-pit targets in the Abitibi, aligning with the A-zone historic grade of ~1.52 g/t Au. The 19.2 g/t Au over 0.51 metres interval in N2-25-012 is bonanza grade but extremely narrow; without a reported estimated true width, it implies selective mining and limited contribution to bulk-tonnage economics. All zones remain open along strike and at depth, with the A-zone offering up to 8 km of potential strike.

before.context: The Disley Project sits in the established Saskatchewan potash corridor with access to rail, power, and workforce, but unlike conventional underground or legacy solution mines, Buffalo Potash plans to use its proprietary HLD selective dissolution method. The reported ~35% KCl grade sits well above typical Saskatchewan sylvinite ore grades of roughly 20–30% KCl, giving it a material grade advantage if the mine-modification factor and metallurgical assumptions hold up. The PEA is classed as AACE Class 4 (±20–30% accuracy), so capital and operating estimates will require refinement in the upcoming Feasibility Study.
before.grade_commentary: A resource grade of 34–35% KCl (22% K2O) is considered exceptionally high for Saskatchewan potash; typical sylvinite ore grades in the basin range from roughly 20% to 30% KCl. At this grade, the brine feed to the crystallizer would be richer than many conventional operations, supporting lower relative operating costs. However, the deposit is solution-mined, so the reported in-situ grade is subject to the mine modification factor (70% recovery including anomaly and process losses), meaning the effective plant feed grade depends on dissolution efficiency and seam selectivity.
before.key_facts: ["Mineral Resource of 1.67 billion tonnes Measured & Indicated grading 34.84% KCl (22.0% K2O), plus 2.66 billion tonnes Inferred at 34.96% KCl — exceptionally high-grade for Saskatchewan potash and supports low-cost solution mining.","Base-case economics show combined after-tax NPV8 of $1.085 billion, 30% IRR, and 4.7-year payback from IPM start; the standalone IPM phase yields $195M NPV8 with 104% IRR and payback in just over 12 months.","Development plan uses patented Horizontal Line-Drive selective solution mining targeting only high-grade seams, with a staged 125,000 t/a IPM to confirm mining and processing assumptions before building two 500,000 t/a plants."]

before.summary: Arizona Gold & Silver announced positive column leach test results from its Philadelphia Project, with HPGR crushing to -6.3mm achieving 76% gold recovery and 40% silver recovery after 119 days — a 16% improvement in gold recovery over conventional crushing. The company also resumed core drilling to test the Perry Vein 60 metres north of the previously reported high-grade intercept of 20.43 metres grading 9.04 g/t Au and 34 g/t Ag. The results support evaluating a potential heap-leach open-pit operation to complement underground development of the higher-grade material.
before.context: Heap-leach operations in the southwestern U.S. commonly process low-grade oxide material in the 0.3–1.5 g/t Au range using multi-lift pads, making the 0.4–1.5 g/t Au stockwork at Philadelphia typical bulk-tonnage feed; achieving >75% recovery at -6.3mm crush with HPGR is competitive with similar regional projects. The 9.04 g/t Au over 20.43m is more typical of underground mine feed than open-pit heap leach, suggesting a potential two-tiered mining scenario.
before.grade_commentary: The 9.04 g/t Au over 20.43 metres in PC25-156 is high-grade for an epithermal system and represents excellent width, supporting underground potential; by comparison, the near-surface stockwork material grading 0.4–1.5 g/t Au is typical for bulk-tonnage, low-grade heap-leach deposits in the southwestern U.S., where 76% recovery via HPGR crushing is a positive economic indicator at current gold prices.
before.key_facts: ["Hole PC25-156 previously intersected 20.43 metres grading 9.04 g/t Au and 34 g/t Ag — a result more than six times the surrounding near-surface stockwork grades of 0.4–1.5 g/t Au and the direct target for new step-out hole PC25-157.","Column leach tests after 119 days show HPGR crushing to -6.3mm yields 76% gold recovery and 40% silver recovery, outperforming conventional crushing by 16% on gold and 12% on silver along a nearly linear leach curve.","The near-surface stockwork material is amenable to heap-leach extraction; the company is targeting 80% total gold recovery within 150 days and evaluating a potential open-pit heap-leach operation alongside underground development of the higher-grade zones."]

before.summary: Artemis Gold’s board has approved a $1.44 billion expanded Phase 2 (EP2) development at its Blackwater Mine in BC, which will increase processing capacity to 21 Mtpa and target average annual production of 500,000–525,000 ounces of gold for the first 10 full years. The company expects to fund EP2 primarily from operating cash flow and its strengthened balance sheet, emphasizing no equity dilution is required, though the final investment decision remains conditional on BC Hydro confirmation in early 2026. Early works are set for January 2026, major construction for Q3 2026, and first gold pour is expected in Q3 2028.
before.grade_commentary: Blackwater’s resource and reserve grades of 0.61–0.75 g/t Au are low-grade by conventional standards and are only economic due to the massive 21 Mtpa bulk open-pit scale; at this throughput and guided AISC of US$800–US$1,100/oz, the deposit generates exceptional margins at current gold prices.

before.context: Saskatchewan potash deposits typically average 20–25% KCl in mill feed; Disley’s ~35% KCl grades are in the top tier globally. before.context: The Storm Project is a sediment-hosted copper system in Nunavut where Aston Bay holds a 20% free-carried interest until a bankable feasibility study is completed. For open-pit copper projects globally, feed grades typically run below 1% Cu, making the 5–8% Cu intervals reported here exceptional; the 27.3% Cu grade is bonanza territory rarely seen outside narrow high-grade vein systems.
before.grade_commentary: 27.3% Cu is bonanza-grade and exceptional for any copper deposit type. The broader 12.1m @ 5.6% Cu and 3.8m @ 8.1% Cu intervals are thick, high-grade intercepts that far exceed typical open-pit copper mine feed grades (usually 0.4–1.0% Cu). The reported widths are downhole lengths interpreted by the company to be close to true widths; the 0.5m @ 27.3% Cu interval is narrow but occurs within a much wider mineralized envelope, suggesting strong metal endowment rather than a discrete uneconomic vein.

after.context: Junior explorers often rebrand after divesting flagship assets to pivot toward new opportunities, but the proposed 18 million option issuance, concentrated among three insiders and equivalent to roughly 16% of existing shares, is unusually dilutive and will test shareholder support for the new LE Minerals strategy.

before.summary: Lithium Universe announced that a Macquarie University Life Cycle Assessment confirmed its Silver Extraction PV Recycling Project (SEPR) achieves an 85% reduction in carbon emissions and 83% less nitric acid use compared to conventional silver recovery. The Jet Electrochemical Silver Extraction (JESE) process extracts 97.1% of silver in four minutes at 99.88% purity, with a parallel techno-economic analysis indicating revenue exceeding US$2,500 per kilogram of silver recovered—more than triple conventional methods. While the results highlight a potentially disruptive environmental and economic advantage, the technology remains pre-commercial with no immediate revenue or offtake agreements disclosed.

before.context: Iron Duke is located within 15 km of Locksley's Tottenham Project in the Cobar district of NSW, a region known for shear-hosted copper-gold deposits. The 1.0–1.5% Cu grades and exceptional 4.48 g/t Au hit compare favourably to typical Cobar lode systems, though the resource remains Inferred and is based largely on 2012-era drilling.
before.grade_commentary: The reported copper grades of 1.0–1.5% Cu are moderate to high for shear-hosted lode deposits in the Cobar region and would be considered robust feed if ultimately mined. The standout 13 m @ 1.56% Cu and 4.48 g/t Au from KIDRC009 is exceptional, representing bonanza-grade gold credit within a copper-gold system. True widths are estimated at 65–85% of drilled widths due to the steep 60–80° easterly dip of the mineralisation; the system remains open to the south and at depth.

before.grade_commentary: The resource average of 1.0% Cu is moderate-to-high for a shear-hosted lode system, with select historical intercepts such as 1.56% Cu and 4.48 g/t Au representing genuinely high-grade shoots. True widths are estimated at 65–85% of drilled widths given steeply-dipping mineralisation (60–80° ESE) versus hole dips of 50–60° WNW, meaning the best intercepts translate to roughly 8–20 metre true widths. Surface rock chips from the Christmas Gift prospect assayed up to 26.1% Cu, but these are grab samples and not representative of in-situ grade continuity.
