before.grade_commentary: The 1.84 g/t Au diluted Indicated grade is moderate for an underground deposit — economic in a US$3,500/oz gold environment but below the 3.0 g/t threshold used when gold was $1,800/oz. This is a deliberate departure from Fremont's historical 10.7 g/t Au production, trading grade for scale and mineability.

before.grade_commentary: The broader intercepts of 9m @ 1.27 g/t Au and 15m @ 1.46 g/t Au represent moderate, low-moderate grades appropriate for bulk open-pit mining in the WA goldfields and align with the Exploration Target. The internal high-grade intervals of 1m @ 6.55 g/t Au and 2m @ 4.34 g/t Au are encouraging but narrow, suggesting localised high-grade shoots within a wider mineralised envelope. The filing ambiguously states true width at Gidgee Flat is estimated at 70–80% of true width, which likely intends that estimated true width is roughly 70–80% of the downhole intercept. Both broad zones remain open along strike and at depth pending further assays.

before.context: Tailings reprocessing projects in the WA Goldfields are increasingly attractive due to lower capex and permitting requirements compared with greenfield mines; the Paris tailings grades of 1.5–4.7 g/t Au sit comfortably above typical heap-leach cut-offs and are comparable to the historical Paris mill feed grade of 2.8 g/t Au. The project’s location 27–35 km from the Higginsville and St Ives processing hubs provides potential toll-treating avenues, though haulage economics and final tonnage estimates remain unverified.
before.grade_commentary: For tailings and stockpile reprocessing, grades of 1.5–4.7 g/t Au are moderate to high and potentially economic given the material is at surface and amenable to cyanide leaching with recoveries up to 98%. The North East Dam intercept of 3m at 4.66 g/t Au stands out as notably higher grade, approaching the historical HHH ore grade of 4.19 g/t Au. Vertical drilling through the flat-lying tailings dams means drilled widths approximate true widths, and the 6–8m thicknesses across the South West Dam represent bulk-tonnage targets well suited to low-cost reclamation.
before.key_facts: ["Macro Mining Services will recover all project expenses from Paris Gold Mine revenue before sharing remaining profit 50:50 with Austral Pacific, effectively free-carrying the vendor.","Historical 2016 Gold Fields AC drilling of the North East Tailings Dam returned intercepts including 3m at 4.66 g/t Au from surface (16AC030) and 3m at 4.25 g/t Au (16AC032), while the South West Dam returned multiple 6–8m intercepts grading 1.84–2.5 g/t Au from surface.","Recent column leach metallurgical testwork achieved 97.91% gold recovery after 27 days on a 2.3 g/t Au oxide composite, with 77–89% recoveries on other tailings composites, supporting potential for economic reprocessing."]

before.grade_commentary: The 1m @ 27.2 g/t Au and 1m @ 10.9 g/t Au intercepts are bonanza grades, while 5m @ 6.02 g/t Au and 2m @ 5.00 g/t Au are clearly high-grade. However, all results are historical down-hole lengths with unknown true widths and were generated using a mix of aqua regia and fire assays; aqua regia can under-report coarse gold. Most of the higher-grade intervals are narrow (1–2m), implying selective mining potential, whereas broader zones such as 10m @ 1.57 g/t Au could support bulk-tonnage targets if proven continuous at depth and along strike.

before.grade_commentary: 0.10–0.19% Cu is low grade for a porphyry copper-gold deposit and would be considered sub-economic if representative of mineable material; however, the 36-metre width suggests a broad alteration halo typical of porphyry systems. The 0.5 g/t Au over 4 metres at Barina is moderate by gold standards and pales against the nearby historic intercept of 204 g/t Au. Estimated true widths are not currently known and down-hole lengths are reported.

before.context: Mt Boppy is a historic high-grade gold mine (~500,000oz at ~15g/t Au), so the lack of significant gold in the first deeper holes since acquisition is a disappointment, though the structural insights may aid future targeting. Pipeline Ridge's 1.1–1.5g/t Au shallow oxide target is more typical of bulk open-pit feed and aligns with Manuka's strategy to diversify ore sources for the Wonawinta plant.
before.grade_commentary: The new Mt Boppy intersections are described by the company as 'localised low-grade gold' and represent a material step-down from the historical ~15g/t Au average that underpinned past production; sulphide mineralisation including up to 46g/t Ag was intersected, but this is not sufficiently high-grade to be economic as a primary driver. The Pipeline Ridge exploration target of 1.1–1.5g/t Au is low-moderate by global standards but appropriate for shallow, free-milling oxide open-pit material that could be profitably processed through Wonawinta if volumes and metallurgy prove favorable.

before.context: The 1.32Moz Ouarigue resource at 1.54 g/t Au places Ferké in the bulk-tonnage, open-pit camp typical of West African Birimian greenstone belts. The broad ETW widths (45–75m) and moderate-to-high grades compare favourably to other Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso development-stage gold projects.
before.grade_commentary: The broad intercepts of 2.52–2.69 g/t Au over 56–75m ETW are well above the 1.54 g/t Au MRE average and represent excellent bulk-tonnage open-pit widths. Internal bonanza-grade intervals including 2.8m @ 11.1 g/t Au (ETW 1.9m) and 8m @ 9.29 g/t Au indicate high-grade shoots within the broader mineralised intrusion. These grades are exceptional for the deposit type, though the very narrow ETW of the 11.1 g/t interval (1.9m) represents a selectively minable vein within a bulk mining envelope.
before.what_to_watch: Watch for regional RC drill results from the 37km Léraba trend; an updated Ouarigue MRE incorporating these assays; and progress on the Ferké South permit grant — all ahead of the targeted Q4 2026 pre-feasibility study completion.

before.summary: Marimaca Copper reported new step-out drill results from its Pampa Medina sediment-hosted copper project in Chile, with hole SPRD-06 intersecting five high-grade stacked mantos across a mineralized package exceeding 400m in thickness. The best intervals include 8m of 2.54% Cu and 21.0 g/t Ag within a broader 22m zone and 32m of 1.02% Cu, with true widths estimated at 80–90% of drilled widths. Step-out holes SPRD-02 and SWRD-05 extended mineralization over 300m from prior drilling, supporting management’s view that Pampa Medina has district-scale potential.
before.grade_commentary: These are high-grade intercepts for a sediment-hosted copper-silver system. Copper grades above 1.5% are considered high, and multiple mantos exceed 2% Cu (peaking at 4.14% Cu over 2m in SPRD-06) with correlated silver up to 50.5 g/t Ag. True widths at 80–90% of drilled width mean the mantos remain thick and mineable, while the vertical stacking of five high-grade horizons in a single hole is a hallmark of tier-one districts like Kamoa-Kakula.
before.what_to_watch: Watch for further assays from the southwestern step-out lines testing extensions through the upper volcanics and sediments, plus the planned northern and western drill lines. Also monitor for a maiden mineral resource estimate once drilling density is sufficient — the company currently notes spacing is inadequate for Inferred or Indicated classification.

after.summary: Marimaca Copper reported new step-out drill results from its Pampa Medina sediment-hosted copper project in Chile, with hole SPRD-06 intersecting five high-grade stacked mantos across a mineralized package exceeding 400m in thickness. The best intervals include 8m of 2.54% Cu and 21.0 g/t Ag within a broader 22m zone and 32m of 1.02% Cu, with true widths estimated at 80-90% of drilled widths. Step-out holes SPRD-02 and SWRD-05 extended mineralization over 300m from prior drilling, supporting management's view that Pampa Medina has district-scale potential.
after.grade_commentary: These are high-grade intercepts for a sediment-hosted copper-silver system. Copper grades above 1.5% are considered high, and multiple mantos exceed 2% Cu (peaking at 4.14% Cu over 2m in SPRD-06) with correlated silver up to 50.5 g/t Ag. True widths at 80-90% of drilled width mean the mantos remain thick and mineable, while the vertical stacking of five high-grade horizons in a single hole is a hallmark of tier-one districts like Kamoa-Kakula.

Silver credits of 10–50 g/t Ag add meaningful by-product value, particularly in the high-grade copper zones.

before.grade_commentary: The reported grades are exceptional by shear-hosted gold standards: 20.5 g/t Au and 10.04 g/t Au are bonanza-grade (>10 g/t), while broader intervals such as 6.0m @ 3.72 g/t Au and 7.0m @ 4.9 g/t Au are high-grade. However, almost all intersections are reported as down-hole lengths; true widths (ETW) are not stated except for VLLD027, which is explicitly noted as ‘not true width, drilled down-dip’. Given the moderate to steep easterly dips (35°–75°), true widths are likely narrower than drilled widths in some holes. The shallow depth of mineralisation (starting at 25m) supports open-pit potential, but the geometry and any narrow true widths may influence mining method selection.

before.summary: MB Gold reported initial assays from its maiden RC drill program at the Twin Veins gold prospect in Western Australia's Pilbara. The standout result was 20 metres of 1.74 g/t gold including a higher-grade 7 metres of 4.06 g/t gold — the widest meaningful intercept recorded at the prospect so far. All six reported holes returned gold, with 14 more holes currently in the lab and a Phase 2 program planned for August.
before.grade_commentary: True widths are estimated at 80–90% of drilled widths, implying the 20m broad envelope equates to roughly 16–18m ETW and the 7m high-grade core to roughly 5.6–6.3m ETW. While 4.06 g/t Au is high grade, the broader 1.74 g/t Au envelope is moderate; for a narrow-vein quartz system, these widths are encouraging but the mineralisation appears to occur as multiple steeply dipping lenses rather than a single continuous vein.

before.context: These results sit along the same ~25km Fairway shear that hosts Meeka's Turnberry deposit (690koz @ 2.0 g/t Au) and St Anne's (40koz @ 3.1 g/t Au), with Rosapenna representing a new 670m-long occurrence between them. The broad, lower-grade envelopes (0.5–1.8 g/t Au over 8–17m) are typical of Archean shear-hosted systems, while the 99.14 g/t Au hit indicates potential for high-grade shoots.
before.grade_commentary: The 1m @ 99.14 g/t Au in 26TBRC0023 is bonanza grade and exceptional by any standard, though the exact estimated true width is not stated; drill holes intersect the structure at 60–70°, suggesting true width is only slightly less than the drilled width. The 2m @ 4.59 g/t Au and 3m @ 4.16 g/t Au are high-grade sub-intervals within broader moderate-grade envelopes (0.58–1.83 g/t Au over 8–17m) that sit at or below the Turnberry resource grade of 2.0 g/t Au but are encouraging for a step-out target under shallow cover.

before.summary: MB Gold has reported initial assays from its maiden 6,000m RC drill program at the Twin Veins prospect, highlighted by 20m at 1.74 g/t gold including 7m at 4.06 g/t gold in hole 26MBRC005, plus multiple gold zones in 26MBRC001. The results confirm a gold-mineralised system with true widths estimated at 80–90% of drilled width, and represent the widest significant intercept recorded at Twin Veins to date. A further 14 holes are awaiting assays, with Phase 2 drilling scheduled to commence in August.
before.grade_commentary: The 7m @ 4.06 g/t Au interval is high-grade for a narrow-vein orogenic gold system in the Pilbara, and the broader 20m @ 1.74 g/t Au envelope is the widest significant result reported from Twin Veins to date. True widths are estimated at 80–90% of drilled widths, so the 20m intercept equates to roughly 16–18m true width. The narrower 1m intercepts at 0.64–1.38 g/t Au are low to moderate grade and would require additional context to assess significance. No bonanza-grade intervals (>10 g/t Au) were returned.

before.context: The T-13 intercepts compare favourably to the existing 10.5Mt Inferred Resource at 2.0% CuEq, with infill grades running 2–10x higher than the resource average and suggesting potential for both resource quality upgrade and expansion. The Otavi Mountain Land is a historic high-grade copper jurisdiction, and these results place T-13 in the top tier of global sediment-hosted copper-silver discoveries for grade.
before.grade_commentary: These grades are exceptional by any copper standard: anything above 1.5% Cu is considered high-grade, while T13DD005a's 50m at >7.9% CuEq and 16.3m at 19.81% CuEq are bonanza-grade. Estimated true widths are strong at 60–90% of drilled width (e.g., T13DD005a ETW ~42.5m), indicating a robust, thick mineralised zone rather than a narrow vein. Several reported CuEq values are conservative because pending silver assays were treated as zero and silver is capped at 200g/t in some cases; native copper intervals also remain un-assayed, suggesting upside to these already remarkable numbers.
before.key_facts: ["T13DD005a returned 50m at 5.55% Cu and >125g/t Ag (>7.9% CuEq) from 194m, including 16.3m at 12.99% Cu and 360.2g/t Ag (19.81% CuEq) — the best intercept yet reported from T-13 and roughly 4x the existing 2.0% CuEq Inferred Resource grade.","T13DD010 delivered multiple high-grade intercepts in one hole over a 40.1m zone: 3.1m at 7.86% Cu and 212.1g/t Ag (11.88% CuEq), 3.9m at 6.99% Cu and 174.1g/t Ag (10.30% CuEq), and 2.5m at 6.13% Cu and 58.6g/t Ag (7.23% CuEq), with true width estimated at ~90% of drilled width.","Silver assays are pending or capped at 200g/t for numerous intervals, and native copper zones in several holes await screen assays — meaning reported CuEq values are conservative; 11 additional drill holes are pending results."]

before.verdict_reason: Exceptional infill intercepts — including bonanza-grade cores well above 2x the Inferred resource grade — confirm broad high-grade continuity at T-13 Main and reveal a new higher-grade West Zone 600m away, materially de-risking and expanding the deposit.
before.grade_commentary: These are exceptional results. Copper grades up to 13.53% Cu and silver grades up to 389.2 g/t Ag are bonanza-grade, while the broad true widths — approximately 35 to 43 metres for the main intervals — are very mineable. The high-grade internal shoots (true widths of roughly 7 to 12 metres) are thick enough to support highly valuable selective mining. Even the broader envelope grades of ~2.5–3.0% Cu over 35+ true metres sit comfortably above open-pit thresholds and are far superior to the 1.6% Cu Inferred resource grade.
before.key_facts: ["T13DD005a returned 50.6m at 7.81% CuEq (5.25% Cu and 135.3g/t Ag), including a bonanza-grade 14.4m at 20.9% CuEq (13.53% Cu and 389.2g/t Ag) — more than ten times the deposit’s 2.0% CuEq Inferred resource grade.","Multiple Main Zone infill holes delivered several +4% CuEq intercepts in single holes: T13DD009 hit 46.2m at 4.01% CuEq with internal zones of 10.6m at 7.45% CuEq and 9.7m at 6.55% CuEq; T13DD010 hit 39.3m at 4.01% CuEq with 7.3m at 8.10% CuEq and 5.7m at 8.30% CuEq; and T13DD013 hit 41.9m at 3.70% CuEq with 11.6m at 7.90% CuEq.","The first infill hole on the T-13 West Zone, 600m west of the Main Zone, intersected 27.0m at 1.46% CuEq (ETW ~17.6m), confirming a second higher-grade lode and indicating the 1.4km strike deposit has room to grow beyond the 10.5Mt Inferred resource."]

before.grade_commentary: The reported rock chip values — including 54.5% Pb, 7.23% Cu and 73.48 g/t Ag — are bonanza grades for any deposit type, but these are selective grab samples from surface outcrop/historic workings and do not represent drilled width or true thickness. SEDEX deposits can be among the world's largest base metal accumulations, but economic viability depends on wide, continuous mineralisation at depth rather than localized high-grade rock chips. No drilled width or ETW is available until auger results are reported.

before.context: These CaF2 grades are significant for carbonatite-hosted fluorspar and compare favorably to typical open-pit feed grades globally, though they fall well below the >97% CaF2 acid-spar specification and would require beneficiation. The Mallard Prospect's proximity to the Ashram Deposit—one of the world's largest fluorspar deposits—offers potential development synergies, but investors should note that historical fluorine assays were selectively performed where fluorite was visually identified, potentially biasing results toward mineralized intervals.
before.grade_commentary: Fluorspar intercepts grading 25–40% CaF2 over 9–32m widths are high-grade for carbonatite-hosted mineralization, but investors should note that historical fluorine assays were selectively performed where fluorite was visually identified, potentially biasing results toward mineralized zones. Beneficiation would be required to reach acid-spar (>97% CaF2) or met-spar (>60% CaF2) product specifications. Associated 0.2–0.4% Nb2O5 offers minor by-product credit potential. True widths are not reported.

before.summary: Neometals announced a maiden JORC 2012 Exploration Target for its 51%-owned Utah Brine Project, outlining conceptual potential of 94–325 Mt of muriate of potash and 1.9–6.5 Mt of lithium carbonate equivalent (100% basis) derived from historical oil and gas well data. The target is explicitly not a Mineral Resource, and the company has not yet conducted its own drilling or sampling, with planned work programs including brine sampling and Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) testing in H2 2026 to validate the dataset. Tenure is substantial but not fully secured, with pending potash lease nominations and prospecting permit applications.
before.grade_commentary: Brine lithium concentrations in the Paradox clastic zones average 55–147 mg/L Li, with an unvalidated historical hit of 340 mg/L Li excluded from the target as a conservative measure; these are moderate grades relative to world-class South American salares but are in line with other U.S. oilfield brine projects. Potassium concentrations up to ~25,037 mg/L are used in the high-case scenario. Economic viability hinges entirely on Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) performance, as traditional evaporation is likely unsuitable for these deeper, lower-grade brines.

before.summary: New Frontier Minerals announced a joint site visit with Austral Resources to the NWQ Copper Project, confirming Big One stockpile material achieves 83–99% acid-soluble copper recovery and is compatible with Austral’s Mt Kelly acid-leach flowsheet. The team also reconnoitred the historical Mt Storm prospect, which reportedly produced ~1,100 tonnes at 6% Cu in small-scale past mining, and collected scout rock-chip samples to characterise the high-grade oxide mineralisation. NFM is now progressing a mining lease application at Big One and advancing the toll-treatment MOU with Austral as a potential low-capex route to production.
before.grade_commentary: 1.1% Cu at Big One is moderate grade for copper, suitable for low-cost acid leach given the >95% acid-soluble recovery, but not exceptional in a global context. The Mt Storm historical grade of 6% Cu is bonanza-grade — more than four times the high-grade threshold — but relates to ~1,100 tonnes of historical small-scale production with no modern drill confirmation; pending rock chip assays will indicate whether similar mineralisation persists. The 1.0–1.2% Cu insitu resource grades are reasonable for oxide/supergene deposits in the region but would need scale and metallurgical continuity to support toll-treatment economics.
before.what_to_watch: Watch for laboratory assay results from the Mt Storm rock chip program (expected in 1–2 months), progress on the Big One Mining Lease Application, and any definitive agreement or expansion of the Austral Resources toll-treatment MOU.

before.summary: Nexus Minerals announced the first tranche of RC drilling results from the Clement Prospect at its Wallbrook Gold Project, with all 10 holes returning anomalous gold intercepts in a stacked multi-lode geometry. before.grade_commentary: 2.1% TREO is an exceptional grade for a heavy rare earths deposit — most global REE projects report grades below 1% TREO. The 94% HREO/TREO ratio confirms strong heavy rare earth dominance (dysprosium and terbium), and the upgrade to ~90% Indicated materially improves geological confidence for the Wolverine-Dazzler blending study. However, the relatively small 340 kt tonnage means Dazzler is best suited as high-grade satellite feed to boost head grades at the larger Wolverine operation, not as a standalone mine.

before.summary: Norwest Minerals released a revised ASX announcement adding JORC-compliant metallurgical details, drill hole collar data, and updated Competent Person statements to its earlier 8 May 2026 release. Bottle roll tests on Bulgera oxide and transition composites achieved 86–92% gold recovery at coarse 25 mm/12.5 mm crush sizes with low reagent use, supporting heap leach viability. The company has appointed Orelogy to lead the Bulgera Heap Leach Scoping Study and commenced column leach testing to validate commercial-scale recoveries.
before.context: Heap leach development scenarios in Western Australia typically target grades between 0.5–1.0 g/t Au, so Bulgera’s 0.65 g/t Au resource sits in the viable range for low-cost, bulk-tonnage extraction, especially with recoveries exceeding 85% at coarse crush. The project is located 50 km northeast of the Plutonic Gold Mine (Catalyst Metals), offering potential infrastructure leverage.
before.grade_commentary: The 0.65 g/t Au resource grade is low but typical for bulk-tonnage heap leach operations; the 86–92% bottle-roll recoveries at a coarse 25 mm crush are excellent and indicate strong heap leach amenability, though column leach confirmation is still required to validate full-scale performance.
before.key_facts: ["Bottle roll tests on oxide and transition composites achieved 86% to 92% gold recovery at coarse crush sizes (25 mm and 12.5 mm), with 75–80% recovery within 72 hours and low reagent consumption averaging 0.38 kg/t cyanide and 1.3 kg/t lime.","The 2026 Bulgera Mineral Resource totals 23.8 Mt @ 0.65 g/t Au for 501,000 oz, a 2.8× tonnage increase from the prior 8.4 Mt estimate, driven by a lower 0.24 g/t cut-off aimed at capturing heap-leachable material.","Column leach testing is now underway at ALS, and Orelogy Mining Consultants have been appointed to lead the Bulgera Gold Heap Leach Scoping Study, with an Environmental Approvals Strategy completed by MBS Environmental."]

before.summary: Nouveau Monde Graphite closed a US$309.5M equity package — a US$213.2M private placement to FCC, Investissement Québec and ENI plus the conversion of 52.4M subscription receipts — more than doubling shares outstanding to 329.1M at US$1.84 per share. Combined with previously announced US$335M project credit facilities, the company confirmed the Final Investment Decision to build Phase 2 of its Matawinie graphite mine. Two senior executives were also appointed to lead legal and sustainability.
before.context: This is one of the largest critical-minerals development financings in Canada, pairing a sovereign-wealth-style fund (FCC), provincial capital (IQ), and a major European energy transition player (ENI) with project debt — a capital structure rarely seen outside top-tier battery metals projects. The ~US$644M combined equity-and-debt package is comparable to the funding required for lithium or rare earth construction decisions.

before.summary: OD6 Metals has located the historic Big Jim Fluorspar Lode at its Quinn Project in Nevada, identifying a third high-grade system alongside Mammoth and Horseshoe. Surface mapping and historic data indicate a shallow-dipping, ~2m massive fluorspar vein grading up to 98.6% CaF2 and a footwall breccia of at least 2m grading 40–60% CaF2, with the system open along strike over more than 220m. All results are historic or visual estimates; modern rock samples are pending assay and no drilling has been completed.
before.grade_commentary: 98.6% CaF2 is effectively acid-grade fluorspar — the highest-value product tier used in hydrofluoric acid, battery tech, and semiconductor manufacturing — and is exceptional for a raw vein sample. The ~2m true width of the massive vein and the additional 2m+ of 40–60% CaF2 breccia represent a robust, near-surface target, but the narrow width and shallow dip imply selective mining methods may be required; confirmation of geometry and consistency via drilling is essential.
before.key_facts: ["Historic channel and rock samples from the Big Jim lode report exceptional grades including 98.6% CaF2 (no width reported), 94.4% over 1.5m true width, and 90.8% over 1.8m true width, while the footwall breccia grades 40–60% CaF2 — all well above typical economic fluorspar cut-offs (>20% CaF2)","The lode is exposed across >220m of historic workings and remains open to the north and south, with a shallow westerly dip creating a direct, near-surface drill target beneath the jasperoid cap","Company-collected rock and metallurgical samples have been dispatched to ALS Global in Reno with assays pending, and maiden drilling is yet to commence pending target prioritisation and permitting"]

before.context: The 1.6–2.2 g/t Au open-pit grades are typical of Western Australian bulk-tonnage operations, but the 5.0 g/t Au Golden Pole lode and 3.8 g/t Au Waihi underground reserve are standout high-grade components that should improve margins and fund lower-grade pit feed. before.grade_commentary: Round Dam’s 1.6 g/t Au is low-moderate grade, economic only at scale via bulk open-pit mining with a 9.9 strip ratio and throughput through the 1.2 Mtpa Davyhurst plant. before.summary: Orezone Gold Corporation has released the first drill results from its recently acquired Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec. The initial 2026 surface drilling of the F160 and F134 zones returned multiple high-grade intercepts, including 16.10 g/t Au over 6.7m and 6.47 g/t Au over 21.5m, supporting planned pit expansions and demonstrating down-plunge continuity for potential underground mining. True widths are estimated at 75–80% of drilled lengths, and mineralization remains open at depth and along strike.
before.context: Casa Berardi has produced over 3.2Moz of gold since 1988 and was most recently operated by Hecla Mining, which drilled 928,969m on the property from 2014–2025. The intercepts align with the mine's historical high-grade underground centers and compare favorably to the current M&I resource grade of 5.93 g/t Au, reinforcing the thesis that near-mine exploration can materially extend mine life.
before.grade_commentary: The reported grades are strong for an orogenic gold system. Intercepts such as 16.10 g/t Au over 6.7m and 6.47 g/t Au over 21.5m (ETW ~16–17m) are well above the ~6 g/t Au resource average and represent high-grade, mineable widths. Bonanza grades including 45.84 g/t Au over 1.8m and 38.02 g/t Au over 0.8m are exceptional but represent narrow vein segments requiring selective mining methods. True widths of 75–80% confirm these are substantive intercepts, not significantly exaggerated by drill angle.
before.what_to_watch: Monitor upcoming drill results from the 118N Zone (~800m depth), where underground drilling has commenced north of the Casa Berardi fault — a largely untested area that could represent a significant new exploration front. Also watch for regular updates from the expanded 40,000–60,000m 2026 program as the company ramps toward 80,000–100,000m annually.

before.summary: Orezone Gold announced the first drill results from its recently acquired Casa Berardi mine in Quebec, returning multiple high-grade intercepts from the F160 and F134 zones. Standout results include 16.10 g/t Au over 6.7m and 6.47 g/t Au over 21.5m (true widths approximately 75–80% of drilled lengths), which support planned pit expansions and demonstrate down-plunge continuity for potential underground mining centers. The company has four exploration rigs operating and plans to ramp up to a sustained 80,000–100,000m per year.
before.grade_commentary: 16.10 g/t Au over 6.7m is bonanza grade and well above the Casa Berardi M&I resource grade of 5.93 g/t Au; the included 45.84 g/t Au over 1.8m is spectacular. The broader 6.47 g/t Au over 21.5m and 7.20 g/t Au over 14.9m intervals are also above the current resource grade and notable for thickness. True widths are 75–80% of drilled lengths, so the 21.5m intercept equates to roughly 16–17m ETW. For an underground orogenic gold deposit, these results are exceptional and support both near-pit expansions and deeper underground targets.
before.what_to_watch: Monitor for ongoing exploration updates as the company ramps drilling toward 80,000–100,000m/yr; upcoming underground results from the 118N Zone (~800m depth); and trade-off study outcomes evaluating an expanded F160 pit versus a transition to underground mining.

before.context: The Okiep Copper District has produced over 100Mt of copper ore historically, and Orion is reviving this South African copper camp. These intercepts rank among the highest-grade copper results reported globally and compare favourably to typical copper mine feed grades of 0.5–1.5% Cu.
before.grade_commentary: The reported 7.88m intercept at 9.24% Cu and the included 3.33m at 17.12% Cu are bonanza grades far exceeding the Flat Mines resource average of 1.3% Cu and global copper mine norms of roughly 0.5–1.0% Cu. Widths are reported as down-hole lengths; true widths are not explicitly stated, though the company indicates holes are drilled close to perpendicular to the steeply north-dipping mineralisation, suggesting reported widths likely approximate true widths. The 3.33m sub-interval is narrower but extraordinarily high-grade, while the overall 7.88m interval provides a meaningful mining width. The mineralisation is open at depth.
before.key_facts: ["New drill hole OFMED157 returned 7.88m at 9.24% Cu, including 3.33m at 17.12% Cu — the 17.12% grade is more than 13 times the Flat Mines resource grade of 1.3% Cu and qualifies as bonanza-grade copper.","The intercept is located 36m down-dip from prior high-grade hits in OFMED154 and 100m along strike from OFMED153, confirming robust continuity of the norite-hosted zone which remains completely open at depth.","The Flat Mines deposits host an existing JORC resource of 10.0Mt at 1.3% Cu (Indicated & Inferred), providing a baseline that these high-grade extensions could materially expand."]

before.summary: Abasca Resources reported winter 2025 assay results from the Loki Flake Graphite Deposit, with multiple holes returning broad intervals grading 8–11% Cg and narrow high-grade zones up to 15.52% Cg—more than double the existing 7.65% Inferred resource grade. The 23-hole program extended inferred-spaced drilling 300m to the northwest and 400m to the southeast, positioning the company to expand the current 11.31 Mt Inferred resource.
before.context: These broad intercepts of 8–11% Cg compare favorably to the global average for flake graphite deposits, which typically run 3–5% Cg, though true widths remain unreported and the high-grade zones require confirmation of continuity.
before.grade_commentary: The broad composites of 8–11% Cg over 20–34m are moderately above the existing 7.65% Inferred resource, suggesting potential for grade uplift in an expanded resource. The narrow included intervals of 15.35–15.52% Cg are exceptional for flake graphite and more than double the deposit average; however, true widths are not reported and these high-grade zones may represent selective intervals requiring confirmation of scale and continuity.

before.summary: Abasca Resources has engaged Tetra Tech to complete a Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) for its 100%-owned Loki Flake Graphite Deposit in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin. The study will incorporate an updated Mineral Resource Estimate reflecting a significantly expanded strike length—from 500 metres to roughly 1,400 metres—following 2025 and 2026 drilling. The PEA will evaluate open-pit mine design, metallurgical recovery, and infrastructure leveraging the project’s proximity to the Key Lake mill site, highway access, and grid power.
before.grade_commentary: A grade of 7.65% Cg is high for a flake graphite deposit. Most global flake graphite operations run on ore grades of 2–5% Cg, meaning Loki’s head grade is comfortably in the upper quartile and should support robust open-pit economics, assuming competitive metallurgical recoveries.
before.key_facts: ["The maiden Inferred resource for the Loki Deposit is 11.31 Mt at 7.65% Cg, a grade that materially exceeds typical flake graphite deposit norms (often 2–4% Cg) and supports strong open-pit potential.","2025 and 2026 infill and extension drilling expanded the delineated strike length from 500 m to approximately 1,400 m, providing a much larger footprint for the updated MRE.","Tetra Tech’s scope includes open-pit mine engineering, a site-specific flotation flowsheet for high-grade flake graphite concentrate, and infrastructure analysis leveraging existing highway and grid power."]

before.grade_commentary: The 2.71% CuEq over 7m (approximately 4.2m to 5.6m ETW) and 4.52% CuEq over 2m (approximately 1.2m to 1.6m ETW) are high-grade intercepts that exceed the B26 Indicated resource grade of 2.08% CuEq. While the 4.52% interval is exceptional, its narrow true width of roughly 1.2–1.6 metres implies a higher-grade lens within a broader envelope that would require selective mining if it persists. The broader 1.81% CuEq over 15m (9–12m ETW) is solidly within the deposit's average grade range and demonstrates robust vertical thickness. All intervals remain open to the west.

before.grade_commentary: 4.04% CuEq (3.63% Cu) over 14 m is exceptional grade for a polymetallic stringer system—roughly double the B26 Indicated resource grade of 2.08% CuEq and over triple on a copper-only basis. The broader 46.7 m envelope at 1.48% CuEq is also well above marginal VMS thresholds. True widths are estimated at 60–80% of drilled length, meaning the 14 m high-grade core likely reflects roughly 8.4–11.2 m ETW (still very mineable), while the bonanza 5.63% CuEq over 2.30 m equates to only ~1.4–1.8 m ETW and would require selective mining. The zone is interpreted to remain open down-plunge and along strike.

before.grade_commentary: A TREO grade of roughly 1,600–1,800 ppm (0.16–0.18%) is very low in conventional mining terms, but for ionic clay deposits the operative metric is the desorbable grade and basket value. The reserve desorbable TREO grade of 465 ppm is economic because the ore is friable surface clay requiring no drilling, blasting, crushing, or grinding, resulting in an operating cost of just US$13.10 per tonne processed and a basket price exceeding US$200 per kilogram of REO. The high proportion of valuable heavy rare earths—particularly Dy and Tb—makes this a high-quality deposit despite the low absolute grade.

before.summary: Central Asia Metals (CAML) will acquire Cygnus Metals (TSXV: CYG) in an all-share scheme of arrangement valuing Cygnus at approximately A$232 million. Cygnus shareholders will receive 0.06 new CAML shares per Cygnus share, a 60% premium to the last close, and will hold roughly 30% of the enlarged group. The deal adds Cygnus’s high-grade Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec—featuring 6.4 Mt at 2.3% Cu and 8.5 Mt at 2.1% Cu—to CAML’s producing base-metal portfolio.
before.context: The 2.3% Cu grade is exceptional by global copper standards—most development projects run below 1.5% Cu—and the deal follows a familiar mid-tier producer playbook of acquiring a high-grade development asset in a top-tier jurisdiction to offset declining reserve life at existing operations. Cygnus itself only consolidated the Chibougamau project in December 2024 through its merger with Doré Copper Mining Corp., making this a rapid second-step transaction.
before.grade_commentary: 2.3% Cu is high-grade copper (well above the 1.5% threshold) and 2.1% Cu in Inferred is similarly strong. The 0.8–1.7 g/t Au and 7.6–7.9 g/t Ag credits are material. These grades support robust underground mining economics and compare favourably to typical open-pit bulk-tonnage copper projects. The historical 900ktpa processing plant on site provides additional strategic infrastructure advantage.

before.summary: Central Asia Metals PLC will acquire Cygnus Metals via an Australian scheme of arrangement at an implied equity value of roughly A$232 million, paying 0.06 CAML shares per Cygnus share — a 60% premium to the last close. The all-share deal hands CAML the high-grade Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec and leaves Cygnus shareholders owning approximately 30% of the combined, cash-generating base metals producer. Closing is targeted for September 2026, subject to court approval, a 75% shareholder vote and regulatory clearances.
before.grade_commentary: The Chibougamau resource grades of 2.3% Cu and 0.8 g/t Au (M&I) — approximately 3.0% copper equivalent — are high-grade for a copper development project and roughly double typical open-pit cutoff grades, though investors should remember these are in-situ resource estimates rather than drilled intercepts.

before.summary: Central Asia Metals (CAML) has agreed to acquire all outstanding shares of Cygnus Metals (TSXV: CYG / ASX: CY5) in a A$232 million all-share transaction. Cygnus shareholders will receive 0.06 new CAML shares for each share held, implying A$0.176 per share — a 60% premium to the last closing price — and will own roughly 30% of the enlarged entity. The deal adds Cygnus's high-grade Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec to CAML's producing assets in North Macedonia and Kazakhstan, with major shareholders representing ~29% of Cygnus already committed to vote in favor.
before.grade_commentary: The 2.3% Cu grade in the M&I resource is high-grade by global copper standards (well above the 1.5% threshold), while the 0.8–1.7 g/t Au provides meaningful by-product credit potential and the 7.6–7.9 g/t Ag adds additional revenue; the resource base supports a potential bulk underground or hub-and-spoke operation.

before.summary: Almadex Minerals provided a 2026 exploration outlook that shifts focus to first-pass drilling across its growing portfolio of early-stage precious and base metal projects in the western USA using its six company-owned drill rigs. The update summarized 2025 generative work—including surface grab samples from Ruby Hill, Big Sky and Red Antler—but disclosed no drill intercepts, resource estimates, or financial figures. The Company expects drilling to restart imminently at the New Hope porphyry target in Arizona while it advances permitting at other projects.
before.grade_commentary: Reported surface grab sample results—including up to 992 g/t silver and 3.5 g/t gold—are encouraging pathfinders for epithermal systems but are not drill intersections and may not represent true underlying mineralisation. No drilled width or true width data is available, and these results cannot be compared to resource or mill feed grades until drill intercepts are reported.

before.verdict_reason: The release does not deliver new drilling or a resource upgrade, but it newly highlights indium potential and an active partner search for Logan, while providing a progress update on the Tim royalty—incremental developments that could affect the investment thesis.
before.grade_commentary: The Logan resource grade of 5.1% Zn is moderate-to-high for bulk-tonnage zinc deposits and supports open-pit potential, while the 23.1 g/t Ag provides a modest precious-metal credit; the indium values (avg 35 ppm, up to 273 ppm) are interesting but generally below the ~100 ppm threshold typical of primary indium deposits, likely offering only a minor byproduct uplift. For the Tim royalty, the historical trench sample of 4.0 m at 468.1 g/t Ag represents bonanza-grade CRD mineralization, but the best 2024 drill intercept of 3.39 m at 52.8 g/t Ag is merely moderate and confirms only that a CRD-style system is present—not yet that it is high-grade at depth.

before.summary: A2 Gold Corp. announced surface channel sampling results from the Blackrock Target at its Eastside project in Nevada, returning up to 10.5 g/t gold and 74.7 g/t silver from narrow basement-hosted quartz veins. The results suggest a potential higher-grade, basement-hosted epithermal vein system distinct from the broader volcanic-hosted mineralization at Castle, though true widths are very narrow at 0.26–0.28 metres. A 7-hole, 2,500 metre drill program is currently underway to test these targets at depth.
before.context: The Blackrock surface results are significantly above the Castle Area inferred resource grade of 0.49 g/t Au and introduce a basement-hosted vein target distinct from the volcanic-hosted dissemination historically drilled at Castle. The narrow true widths (0.26–0.28m) are typical of epithermal vein outcrops but would require confirmation of continuity and width at depth to be economically meaningful.
before.grade_commentary: 10.5 g/t Au is high-grade gold, while accompanying silver values up to 74.7 g/t Ag are moderate. However, the best gold values occur over very narrow true widths (0.26–0.28m), meaning these veins would require selective mining methods if they persist at mineable widths at depth. Surface channels are selective by nature and may not represent in-situ grades or continuity.
before.key_facts: ["Surface channel 1871515 returned 10.50 g/t Au and 33.6 g/t Ag over 0.26m true width — more than 20× the Castle Area inferred resource grade of 0.49 g/t Au.","A second channel, 1871516, assayed 5.63 g/t Au and 68.7 g/t Ag over 0.28m true width, with several other channels returning strongly elevated silver (up to 74.6 g/t Ag over 0.76m).","The existing July 2021 Castle Area inferred resource of 314,000 oz Au at 0.49 g/t Au excludes the Blackrock Target entirely; a 7-hole, 2,500m drill program is now testing depth potential."]

before.grade_commentary: 223 g/t Au is exceptional bonanza grade for any deposit type, and the 7m width is highly significant for an orogenic vein system — far exceeding the narrow vein threshold where selective mining would be required. The intercept is open at depth, and the broader 11m at 144 g/t Au envelope adds confidence that this is not a single isolated vein but a substantial mineralised shoot.

before.context: Tungsten as a by-product credit in orogenic gold systems is uncommon at this scale; while the bulk WO₃ grades of 0.1–0.24% are below typical primary tungsten deposits, the coarse-grained scheelite/ferberite and potential gravity recovery could improve project economics if gold production is established. The 12-shift RC ramp-up signals increasing confidence in the multi-million-ounce gold potential.
before.grade_commentary: The reported tungsten grades are low-to-moderate for a primary scheelite deposit, with bulk intervals of 0.09–0.24% WO₃ typical of large-tonnage, lower-grade systems. However, internal intervals up to 0.9% WO₃ and 11m at 0.55% WO₃ are more encouraging, and the coarse-grained nature of the scheelite/ferberite (amenable to simple panning and potential gravity recovery) means metallurgical testwork could materially upgrade the by-product value. Investors should note these are downhole widths; true widths remain unconfirmed.

before.context: The widespread tungsten anomalism (0.1–0.24% WO3) is modest compared to primary global tungsten operations, but the association with high-grade gold zones running 4–10 g/t Au—well above the 1.0 g/t Au resource grade—and the coarse-grained, gravity-amenable nature of the scheelite/ferberite, could enhance the economics of a future Glenburgh gold operation.
before.grade_commentary: The gold intercepts (4.4–10 g/t Au over 25–79m) are high-grade and approximately 4–10 times the Glenburgh resource grade of 1.0 g/t Au. The tungsten intercepts (0.1–0.24% WO3) are moderate by primary tungsten deposit standards, but the 0.24% WO3 over 26m is a solid by-product interval. The coarse-grained scheelite and ferberite identified by XRD and SEM are amenable to gravity concentration, a low-cost recovery method, though intercepts are reported as downhole lengths and true widths remain unconfirmed.

before.summary: Blue Star Gold has acquired a comprehensive historical exploration dataset for the Sand Lake copper-rich VMS prospect within its Roma Project in Nunavut. Historical drilling from 2003–2008 returned intercepts including 21 metres of 2.71% copper and 6.3 metres of 5.28% copper, with the mineralized horizon interpreted to extend roughly 530 metres along strike. The company has outlined a conceptual exploration target of 3 to 5 million tonnes at 2.3% to 3.6% copper equivalent, but cautions this is not a mineral resource and the historical data has not yet been independently verified.
before.context: Sand Lake sits 12 km north of MMG’s High Lake VMS deposits in the High Lake Greenstone Belt and less than 1 km from the proposed Grays Bay Road corridor. Historical copper grades of 1.5% to 5.7% compare favourably to typical VMS base-case grades of 1–2% Cu, though Blue Star has not yet validated the underlying data.
before.grade_commentary: 5.28% Cu over 6.3m is high-grade for a VMS system and the 21m interval at 2.71% Cu is well above typical VMS thresholds. True widths are estimated at 70–95% of core lengths, meaning these represent thick intervals rather than narrow stringers. However, these are historical assays from 2003–2008 that the Company has not yet independently verified.

before.summary: Patagonia Lithium announced results from a 7km passive seismic survey at its Formentera Lithium Project in Argentina, interpreting the basin basement at roughly 800–1,000m below surface — double the depth of the six existing drill holes. If validated, the deeper basement implies significantly larger brine-hosting aquifer volume beyond the current 551,400t LCE resource. The company is also completing 72-hour pump tests on Wells 2, 3 and 6 and drilling JAM-26-07 to 434m, still within significant gravel intervals.
before.context: Most Argentine salar lithium projects target brines within 200–400m depth; an 800m basement would imply a much larger basin than currently modeled. The 294mg/L average grade is moderate for the Lithium Triangle — economic but below the >600mg/L grades typical of world-class salar operations.
before.what_to_watch: Monitor the 72-hour pump test results from Wells 2, 3 and 6 for flow rate confirmation, and watch whether JAM-26-07 reaches the interpreted 500–550m basement contact to validate the deeper seismic model ahead of an updated Mineral Resource Estimate.

before.summary: K92 Mining announced a major expansion of the AR1 and AR2 high-grade vein zones at its Arakompa project in Papua New Guinea, with all 33 holes intersecting mineralization and bonanza grades up to 164.80 g/t AuEq over true widths of roughly 0.5–1.2 metres. The results also delineated broad near-surface bulk intersections exceeding 140 metres at 1–3 g/t AuEq, advanced a porphyry vector with kilometre-scale alteration intervals, and confirmed that mineralization remains open up-dip to surface and along strike.
before.grade_commentary: Grades above 90 g/t AuEq are bonanza by any standard; however, the ultra-high-grade intervals are narrow (true widths of ~0.54–1.17 m) and would require selective mining methods. They are economically meaningful because they occur within thicker high-grade envelopes averaging 9.47 g/t AuEq over 4.32 m true width and within very broad bulk zones (+100 m at 1–3 g/t AuEq) amenable to conventional open-pit or bulk underground methods. The porphyry CuEq results (0.30–0.35% CuEq over hundreds of metres) are below typical reserve-grade porphyry thresholds but indicate a large, open system with potential to vector into a higher-grade core.
before.key_facts: ["KARDD0084G cut 4.70 m at 41.90 g/t AuEq (2.54 m true width) on the AR2 Vein, including 1.00 m at 164.80 g/t AuEq — a bonanza grade roughly 16× typical underground cut-off thresholds.","KARDD0076 returned multiple high-grade intercepts in a single hole: 11.90 m at 14.30 g/t AuEq (including 1.70 m at 92.43 g/t AuEq), 4.70 m at 6.92 g/t AuEq, and 3.60 m at 6.67 g/t AuEq, demonstrating stacked vein continuity.","The near-surface bulk tonnage zone was significantly expanded with thick intersections such as 177.55 m at 1.01 g/t AuEq in KARDD0100 and 163.50 m at 1.02 g/t AuEq in KARDD0104, underpinning potential for large-scale bulk mining."]

before.summary: Frontier Energy has called a general meeting for 10 July 2026 to seek shareholder approval for a $110 million conditional placement of 550 million shares at $0.20 each, representing a roughly 23–26% discount to recent market prices. before.what_to_watch: Outcome of the 10 July 2026 shareholder vote and whether Frontier secures credit-approved senior debt commitments by early July; if both conditions are met, new shares are expected to settle and begin trading on 15–16 July 2026.

before.grade_commentary: The broad KAI226 intercepts (0.30–0.31 g/t AuEq over 23.5m and 42.1m) are typical of low-grade Au-Cu porphyry mineralization and are reported at roughly 50% estimated true width. The 1.41 g/t AuEq over 1m and 1.74 g/t Au over 3m are locally high-grade pulses but very narrow; they do not yet demonstrate mineable thickness and, in the case of Haddington, were judged too small to be economic.
before.key_facts: ["Reconnaissance hole HAD001 at the Haddington prospect returned 3m grading 1.74 g/t Au and 0.07% Cu from 354m, a high-grade pulse exceeding typical large-scale porphyry norms by more than 2×, though the company considers the target sub-economic with no further work planned.","Deep diamond hole KAI226 in the Boda-Kaiser corridor returned multiple significant intercepts: 1m @ 1.41 g/t AuEq, 23.5m @ 0.31 g/t AuEq incl 3.2m @ 0.53 g/t AuEq, 42.1m @ 0.30 g/t AuEq incl 5m @ 0.53 g/t AuEq and 4.8m @ 0.59 g/t AuEq, intersecting the interpreted magmatic root to the hydrothermal breccia.","A new Mobile Magnetotelluric (MMT) survey defined six high-priority porphyry targets north of Boda-Kaiser—including Driell Creek, Murga, Gollan North, and the newly named One Tree and Old Station prospects—with ground validation commenced and Q3 2026 drilling planned at Driell Creek."]

before.summary: Advance Metals released an amended announcement confirming the maiden drill hole at its Gavilanes silver project in Mexico intersected 33.9 metres at 220 g/t silver, including a bonanza-grade core of 6.2 metres at 718 g/t silver, plus deeper polymetallic zones with copper, lead and zinc. The amendments add Competent Person confirmations and cross-references for the project’s Foreign Estimate and Yoquivo resource but do not change the drill results. Assays are pending for follow-up hole GV-26-002, which tested a southern extension, while a third hole is in progress as part of a 15–18 hole program aimed at supporting a JORC Resource upgrade in early Q4 2026.
before.what_to_watch: Assays from southern extension hole GV-26-002 and ongoing hole GV-26-003; completion of the maiden 15–18 hole (~4,500m) program; and a JORC Mineral Resource upgrade targeted for early Q4 2026. Also monitor for any results from historic core sampling review.

before.context: Nearly all advanced ASX/NYSE-listed rare earth projects — including Mt Weld, Ngualla, Nolans and Yangibana — rely on multi-stage flotation to produce a high-grade concentrate followed by aggressive thermal cracking (acid bake or sulphation). Kameelburg’s ancylite-hosted carbonatite mineralisation appears to be a distinct style that is readily soluble in atmospheric HCl, potentially eliminating an entire beneficiation circuit and the associated capital and energy intensity. The chairperson also cites the project as hosting the world’s largest reported strontium resource.
before.grade_commentary: The ~72% cumulative TREE recovery under ambient, un-optimised conditions on a run-of-mine composite is a strong initial benchmark — materially exceeding the ~43% recovery rate of the Ngualla BFS and achieved without the flotation and acid-bake circuits typical of advanced REE peers. The >99% strontium extraction is exceptional and underpins a potential dual-product revenue stream. However, roughly 28% of the TREE remains in leach residue, likely tied to refractory phosphate or niobate minerals, which the next testwork phase will need to address.
before.key_facts: ["Cumulative ~72% TREE extraction (single-pass 69.2% at 15% HCl) and >99% strontium recovery achieved via direct atmospheric HCl leaching without prior flotation, magnetic separation, or thermal cracking — materially exceeding Ngualla’s ~43% recovery and bypassing unit operations required by most advanced REE peers.","Composite head grade confirmed at 1.28% TREE and 2.67% Sr by XRF; light REE-dominant basket with cerium, lanthanum and neodymium as principal value drivers, offering exposure to magnet rare earth demand.","Multiple clearly defined optimisation pathways identified to lift recovery and reduce costs, including elevated-temperature leaching, QEMSCAN/MLA mineralogical characterisation, pre-concentration (flotation/gravity), residue sulphate-bake trials, and acid-regeneration scoping."]

before.grade_commentary: For a carbonatite-hosted REE deposit, 1.5–2.0% TREO over 136–318 metres is exceptional both in grade and thickness, while 0.40–0.55% Nb₂O₅ over 210-metre intervals is moderate-to-good niobium tenor comparable to producing carbonatite mines. The high strontium credits (4.9–5.2% SrCO₃) add material by-product value that the company equates to roughly an additional 1% TREO. True widths are not reported and remain a key variable for the upcoming resource estimate.

before.summary: Alkane Resources reported exploration results from the Boda–Kaiser corridor and wider Northern Molong Porphyry Project, highlighted by deep drill hole KAI226 cutting a mineralised magmatic-root breccia in the 500m gap between the two deposits. The hole returned multiple intercepts including 1m at 1.41 g/t AuEq and 42.1m at 0.30 g/t AuEq, while a Mobile Magnetotelluric survey generated six new regional targets. Baseline environmental and scoping studies are underway as the company advances the project toward regulatory approval.
before.context: The Northern Molong project sits in the same belt as Newcrest’s Cadia Valley alkalic porphyry cluster, where large, low-grade footprints host higher-grade breccia centres. The Boda–Kaiser resource averages roughly 0.32–0.39 g/t Au and 0.06–0.08% Cu, so the broad widths in KAI226 fit the deposit model but do not represent a step-change in grade.
before.grade_commentary: The broad intercepts of 0.30–0.31 g/t AuEq over 23.5m and 42.1m (ETW ~12m and ~21m respectively) are moderate and consistent with the Boda–Kaiser resource grade, fitting a large porphyry Au-Cu system. The 1m @ 1.41 g/t AuEq (ETW ~0.5m) is bonanza grade but extremely narrow, likely reflecting a selective high-sulphide cement zone within the breccia. The reconnaissance intercept of 3m @ 1.74 g/t Au at Haddington is high-grade but too small to be economic at this stage. Mineralisation remains open along strike and up-dip of KAI226.
before.key_facts: ["Drill hole KAI226 intersected 1m grading 1.41 g/t AuEq (1.37 g/t Au) — a bonanza-grade interval roughly 4× the Boda–Kaiser resource average — within a newly identified magmatic-root breccia between the two deposits.","The same hole reported multiple intercepts above the 0.3 g/t AuEq threshold: 42.1m @ 0.30 g/t AuEq, 23.5m @ 0.31 g/t AuEq, 4.8m @ 0.59 g/t AuEq, 5m @ 0.53 g/t AuEq and 3.2m @ 0.53 g/t AuEq (ETW ~50%).","A Mobile Magnetotelluric survey identified six new high-priority porphyry targets, with a deep drill hole at Driell Creek planned for Q3 2026."]

after.context: The modest working-capital raise is typical for TSXV explorers advancing a flagship asset, but the insider participation and proximity to OceanaGold's producing Haile Gold Mine (170,000-200,000 oz Au/year) underscore strategic optionality for the Brewer Project.

before.context: Brewer is a large, underexplored Au-Cu system with near-surface epithermal mineralization and deeper porphyry potential, situated near OceanaGold's Haile operation which has 2025 production guidance of 170,000–200,000 ounces of gold.

after.context: Brewer is a large, underexplored Au-Cu system with near-surface epithermal mineralization and deeper porphyry potential, situated near OceanaGold's Haile operation which has 2025 production guidance of 170,000-200,000 ounces of gold.

before.context: Brewer sits 13 km from OceanaGold's producing Haile Gold Mine and already hosts a near-surface epithermal gold resource, but these results represent the first systematic test for deeper porphyry copper-gold potential — a deposit style that typically requires multiple drill campaigns to define and often carries grades >0.3% Cu, well above the anomalous 183–490 ppm Cu reported here.
before.grade_commentary: The reported copper values (183–490 ppm, or 0.018%–0.049% Cu) are geochemically anomalous relative to background (<50 ppm) but are far below economic thresholds for porphyry copper deposits (typically >0.3% Cu). The 410-meter width is encouraging as a vector, but at these grades the interval does not represent ore and would not be economic even with the 0.75–1.0 g/t Au epithermal grades common at Brewer. The significance lies in the chalcopyrite and B-type veining, which are classic porphyry pathfinders.
before.what_to_watch: Pending assay results from Holes 38 and 39 — particularly Hole 38, drilled 750m to the northwest to test the refined porphyry target — and OceanaGold's progression toward its US$1.5 million initial spend commitment (expected Q2 2026) and US$8 million earn-in milestone by December 2027.
before.key_facts: ["Hole 37 (B26C-037) returned multiple anomalous copper intervals totaling 410m averaging 183 ppm Cu from 198m depth, including 78m at 260 ppm Cu and 14m at 490 ppm Cu — all hosted in chalcopyrite and representing a distinct higher-temperature assemblage from Brewer's known near-surface mineralization","Reinterpretation of the MT-IP anomaly indicates it reflects a peripheral alteration zone rather than a causative intrusive body, refining the exploration vector toward higher-priority areas to the northwest where alteration thickens","Assays for Holes 38 and 39 are pending; Hole 38 was collared approximately 750m northwest of Hole 37 to specifically test the revised porphyry target under the earn-in partnership with OceanaGold"]

before.summary: Cartier Resources announced metallurgical test results from the Main Sector of its 100%-owned Cadillac project in Val-d’Or, showing average gold extraction of 96.3% via conventional cyanide leaching—up from 93.1% assumed in the 2023 PEA and 90.6% historical Chimo production. The results demonstrate low reagent consumption, low sulfur content, and moderately hard ore, suggesting a simple, conventional processing route. The company also disclosed it is planning initial metallurgical tests on the North Contact gold zone.
before.context: The 96.3% recovery is exceptional for non-refractory gold ore in the Abitibi and materially exceeds the 2023 PEA assumption, implying lower processing risk and better project economics than previously modeled. Typical operating gold mines in the region target 92–95% recovery, and the low cyanide consumption adds further operating cost appeal.

before.summary: Cartier Resources announced the twelfth set of drill results from the Main sector at its 100%-owned Cadillac project in Val-d'Or, Quebec. The results confirm multiple parallel, near-surface gold zones over roughly 1.7 km, highlighted by broad intervals such as 2.1 g/t Au over 19.1 m and 1.4 g/t Au over 16.0 m, with included bonanza-grade sections up to 19.6 g/t Au over 1.0 m. Estimated true widths are 55–90 % of reported core lengths.
before.context: The Cadillac Project sits on the Cadillac Fault in the Val-d'Or camp, one of Quebec's most prolific gold belts. The broad, near-surface envelopes and networks of higher-grade quartz shoots are typical of Abitibi shear-hosted systems, where 2–3 g/t Au resources are often mined underground.
before.grade_commentary: The broad 10–19 m intercepts grading 1.1–2.1 g/t Au are moderate in grade but align with the project’s 2.4 g/t Au Indicated resource, and their shallow vertical depths (~25–200 m) are favorable for bulk mining. Included intervals up to 19.6 g/t Au over 1.0 m are bonanza-grade, roughly eight times the resource grade; however, estimated true widths are 55–90 % of reported core length, meaning the 1.0 m included intervals translate to approximately 0.55–0.90 m true width. The 0.7 m included intercept in CA26-341 (6.9 g/t Au) could be narrower than 0.5 m true width, implying very selective mining would be required for the highest-grade veinlets.
before.key_facts: ["Hole CA26-595 intersected 2.1 g/t Au over 19.1 m including 19.6 g/t Au over 1.0 m — the included interval is roughly 8x the project's 2.4 g/t Au Indicated resource grade.","CA26-595 also returned multiple additional high-grade intercepts in the same hole: 4.3 g/t Au over 3.0 m including 9.3 g/t Au over 1.0 m, and 8.5 g/t Au over 1.0 m within the broader 19.1 m interval.","Hole CA26-343 cut 1.6 g/t Au over 12.0 m including 10.7 g/t Au over 1.0 m, while CA26-597 hit 1.4 g/t Au over 16.0 m including 9.8 g/t Au over 1.0 m."]

before.context: The 2.88% CuEq grade is well above the 0.3–0.5% Cu norm for bulk open-pit deposits and rivals many global underground copper-zinc operations. The 68% Indicated weighting is unusually high for a maiden resource, reflecting the density of the 42,000m drill campaign and good geological confidence.
before.grade_commentary: The 2.88% CuEq headline grade is high-grade for any copper deposit and exceptional for a polymetallic system; the Ciclón Mixed Zone at 4.00% CuEq is bonanza-grade. However, true widths vary significantly — while CI-P7M2-01 delivers 19.91m true thickness at 7.90% CuEq, intervals like CI-P10M2-04 have 22.36m drilled widths but only 3.37m true thickness, reflecting steeply dipping vein-breccias that would require selective underground mining. Mineralisation is open at depth and along strike.

before.context: Shallow gold intercepts of 1–2 g/t Au over 7–9m widths are typical of early-stage Kalgoorlie district exploration and are prospective for near-surface, bulk-tonnage open-pit scenarios, though the project currently lacks a JORC resource, metallurgical data, or estimated true width confirmation.
before.grade_commentary: 1.75–1.85 g/t Au is moderate grade for the Kalgoorlie goldfields — respectable for near-surface bulk mining but not bonanza. The 7–9m widths are meaningful if true width is similar, though these are shallow aircore results and the geometry remains early-stage. No estimated true width is disclosed, but the company states intercepts are generally perpendicular to strike; deeper RC results are needed to confirm continuity and width at depth.

before.summary: Aeris Resources has received Supreme Court approval for its scheme of arrangement to acquire 100% of Peel Mining, with implementation expected on 1 July 2026 and new shares to be issued as consideration. The deal adds the South Cobar Copper Project—including the Mallee Bull (122kt Cu at 1.9%) and Wirlong (75kt Cu at 1.75%) deposits—to Aeris’ Tritton operations, significantly increasing the Cobar region resource base. Mallee Bull will be prioritised as a near-term, high-grade feed source for the Tritton mill, with a maiden Ore Reserve slated for Q1 FY27.

before.context: The Boda-Kaiser system is geologically analogous to the Cadia Valley porphyry district but remains at a much earlier stage; these corridor grades of ~0.16–0.17 g/t Au sit below the existing 0.35 g/t Au resource average, implying that while the system is large, further higher-grade confirmation is needed to demonstrate economic continuity between the two deposits.
before.grade_commentary: The KAI226 corridor intercepts of 0.16–0.17 g/t Au and 0.14% Cu over 23.5–42.1m (ETW ~12–21m) are below the existing Boda-Kaiser resource grade of ~0.35 g/t Au and would be considered low-grade in a porphyry context, though they demonstrate continuity of mineralisation in the untested corridor. The 1m @ 1.37 g/t Au interval (ETW ~0.5m) is a high-grade outlier but too narrow for bulk mining. HAD001’s 3m @ 1.74 g/t Au is high grade relative to the deposit average but occurs in a regional prospect the company has deprioritised.
before.key_facts: ["Regional reconnaissance hole HAD001 intersected 3m grading 1.74 g/t Au and 0.07% Cu — roughly 5x the Boda-Kaiser resource average — though true widths are unknown and the company currently has no follow-up plans for this prospect.","Diamond drill hole KAI226 in the Boda-Kaiser corridor returned multiple significant intercepts including 1m @ 1.41 g/t AuEq (1.37 g/t Au, 0.04% Cu), 23.5m @ 0.31 g/t AuEq (0.17 g/t Au, 0.14% Cu), and 42.1m @ 0.30 g/t AuEq (0.16 g/t Au, 0.14% Cu), with estimated true widths ~50% of drilled width; the hole intersected a mineralised magmatic root zone open along strike and up-dip.","The Boda and Kaiser deposits collectively host a 931.7 Mt resource at 0.35 g/t Au and 0.11% Cu for 9.77 Moz Au and 1,038 Kt Cu (Boda updated Dec 2023; Kaiser revised Apr 2024)."]

before.summary: Almonty Industries has requested a voluntary trading halt on its ASX-listed CDIs to facilitate a proposed offering of convertible senior notes in the United States. The halt is intended to keep the company's securities from trading while the note deal is being completed across jurisdictions. Trading is expected to remain paused until the earlier of an announcement on the offering or the commencement of normal trading on approximately 9–10 June 2026.

before.summary: DFR Gold has commenced a feasibility study at its Cascades gold project in Burkina Faso targeting a 20,000–30,000 ounce per annum operation. The company secured US$1 million in unsecured, 8% term loans from its two largest shareholders, who collectively control roughly 77.5% of shares, and also deferred repayment of prior shareholder loans to June 30, 2026. Additionally, DFR paid the remaining US$500,000 to exercise the Wuo Land option, a prerequisite to applying for a mining permit should the feasibility study prove positive.
before.context: The 1.52–1.67 g/t Au grades are typical of small-scale, bulk-tonnage open-pit projects in Burkina Faso, but the economics remain sensitive to metallurgy and capital costs. The resource estimate was prepared using a US$1,900/oz gold price, suggesting potential for material expansion at current prices above US$3,300/oz, though DFR must spend US$18M by September 2026 to preserve its 80% project interest.
before.grade_commentary: 1.52–1.67 g/t Au is low-moderate grade, generally considered economic for bulk open-pit mining in West Africa but highly sensitive to recovery rates, strip ratios, and capital costs; it is below the typical threshold for profitable narrow-vein or underground operations.

before.context: The clean chemistry at Quinn contrasts with major producing deposits globally—such as Las Cuevas in Mexico where arsenic approaches 300 ppm and Silius in Italy which hosts 3.2% lead—suggesting lower environmental and processing risks than typical epithermal fluorspar systems. The U.S. currently imports 100% of its fluorspar and classifies it as a critical mineral, adding strategic context to a potential domestic Nevada source.
before.grade_commentary: Horseshoe's average 70.9% CaF2 is high-grade for raw fluorspar feed and comfortably exceeds the 60% CaF2 MetSpar threshold; the low sulphur (~130 ppm vs a <3,000 ppm threshold) and trace arsenic (23.4 ppm vs <10–20 ppm AcidSpar target) materially de-risk the material for premium product pathways. Mammoth's 40.8% CaF2 is lower grade but still notably cleaner than typical global deposits, though it will require substantial mass reduction via ore-sorting to reach commercial specifications.

before.summary: Vertex Minerals reported May 2026 operations at its high-grade Reward Gold Mine, with 51 ounces of gold sold and 26 ounces on hand, while decline development and rehabilitation advanced ahead of an October 2026 production ramp-up target. The company confirmed an updated JORC resource estimate — supported by a new structural geology model incorporating 30 known gold seams — is expected in early July 2026. Progress continues on procurement of narrow-vein mining equipment and a DA modification to expand underground blasting hours, with determination expected mid-July.
before.context: The Reward deposit's 16.7 g/t Au grade is exceptional for narrow-vein underground mining, far exceeding typical Australian underground grades of 3–6 g/t Au. The mine sits directly beneath the historic Hawkins Hill mine, which produced 435,000 oz at 309 g/t Au, highlighting the district's high-grade endowment.
before.grade_commentary: 16.72 g/t Au is bonanza grade for an underground gold deposit, well above the 5–10 g/t threshold typically considered high-grade. However, current production is from narrow vein structures and development ore, with the company actively working to reduce dilution through narrower drives and selective mining methods.

before.grade_commentary: While not a traditional drill intercept, the metallurgical upgrade is exceptional: a 33x HREE enrichment to 6,161 ppm HREE in the 3.0–3.5 SG band is outstanding for clay-hosted mineralisation. The 72% HREO:TREO ratio far exceeds typical clay REE norms (often <25% HREO) and positions the concentrate as a premium heavy rare earth feed. The parallel +3.5 SG zircon concentrate at 3.14% Zr and 697 ppm Hf adds a second, high-value product without additional mining cost. The extremely low U/Th (max 57 ppm U, 73.5 ppm Th) removes a key logistics and environmental hurdle common in REE projects.

before.summary: Viking Mines has reported a major improvement in metallurgical testwork at its Linka Tungsten Project in Nevada, achieving a premium 62.5% WO3 concentrate grade at 59.8% recovery from a combined gravity and flotation circuit — up from 56.4% WO3 at 46.0% recovery reported in March. The result was replicated on a larger 10 kg sample, de-risking the low-CAPEX gravity-led flowsheet ahead of the maiden drilling programme targeted for the June 2026 quarter. With global APT prices near record highs at US$3,050/mtu, the company is positioning Linka as a potential domestic US tungsten supplier.
before.context: The 62.5% WO3 concentrate grade exceeds the typical >50% WO3 saleability threshold for scheelite concentrate, placing it in the premium product category, while the 59.8% recovery is a meaningful improvement but still short of the 70%+ target the company is pursuing. Historical Linka mine production averaged 0.69–0.98% WO3, though the current 1.2% feed grade comes from loose surface rocks and may not reflect in-situ grades until drilling confirms continuity and scale.
before.key_facts: ["Combined gravity and cleaner flotation circuit achieved 62.5% WO3 concentrate at 59.8% recovery from a 1.2% WO3 feed grade — a significant uplift from the prior 46.0% recovery at 56.4% WO3 reported in March 2026, validated on a larger 10 kg sample.","Standalone gravity concentrate graded 66.6% WO3 at 42.7% recovery, confirming the low-CAPEX gravity-only pathway at five-fold larger scale than previous testwork.","Maiden drilling at Linka remains on track for the June 2026 quarter with permits approved; APT pricing sits near all-time highs at US$3,050/mtu."]

before.summary: Viking Mines has received final US Bureau of Land Management approval for its 63-hole maiden drill program at the Linka Tungsten Project in Nevada, clearing the last federal regulatory hurdle ahead of planned June quarter mobilization. The program will test three priority areas including verification of historic high-grade intercepts such as 8.5m @ 1.0% WO3 — double the project's historical production grade — and maiden drilling on an ~800m southwest extension where surface samples reached 0.6% WO3.
before.context: Linka was acquired as part of Viking's entry into US production-proven tungsten assets; the 1.0% WO3 historical intercept is robust by global tungsten standards, where many operating skarn deposits run at 0.2–0.5% WO3, and Linka's own 0.5% grade supported ~65,000 tonnes of historical output before 1956.
before.grade_commentary: While this filing contains no new assays, the referenced historical intercept of 8.5m @ 1.0% WO3 is a strong grade for a tungsten system — double the project's 0.5% historical production grade and well above typical economic thresholds for skarn-hosted tungsten mineralization.

before.summary: Viridis Mining and Minerals (VMM) has produced its first batch of high-grade Mixed Rare Earth Carbonate (MREC) from its demonstration plant at the Rare Earth Research and Processing Centre in Poços de Caldas, Brazil. The 100kg/hr facility—one of the largest semi-industrial continuous ionic clay rare earth plants outside China—is now processing feed from the Colossus Northern Concessions and producing ~8kg of MREC per day at nameplate capacity. This operational milestone supports sample supply to offtake partners, validates DFS process parameters targeted for completion by end-June 2026, and keeps initial long-lead equipment orders on schedule for Q3 2026.

before.summary: Viridis Mining and Minerals has executed a binding turnkey agreement with municipal distributor DME for a 3.2km, 138kV transmission line to connect the Colossus Rare Earth Project to the Brazilian grid. The contract reserves 27MW of capacity for Stage 1 from December 2027—scalable to 90MVA—at a fixed price of roughly US$0.8M, aligning with the company’s goal of first production in H1 2028. The deal follows recent first mixed rare earth carbonate output from Viridis’ demonstration plant and an offtake LoI with Solvay, with the company now targeting a Final Investment Decision in H2 2026.

before.context: The El Pantano project is located in the Deseado Massif, host to AngloGold's Cerro Vanguardia (approx. 8 Moz Au produced) and Newmont's Cerro Negro (approx. 12 Moz Au). The reported grades (0.1–0.8 g/t Au) are well below those of producing mines in the district, but the structural setting and pathfinder geochemistry suggest potential for discovery of higher-grade feeder zones with additional drilling.
before.grade_commentary: All reported gold intercepts are low-grade (0.1–0.8 g/t Au), which is sub-economic for an epithermal vein system. The best interval (18m at 0.46 g/t Au) is well below typical mineable grades in the Deseado Massif. The presence of broad intervals with anomalous gold and pathfinder elements (arsenic, copper) is encouraging for the system size but does not yet demonstrate economic mineralization. No true thicknesses are provided.

before.summary: ProMIS Neurosciences reported a blinded 6-month interim analysis of its Phase 1b PRECISE-AD trial. No ARIA-E was observed (0%; vs ~12-24% for approved antibodies), total ARIA was 4.4% (all mild ARIA-H), and two key biomarkers—plasma pTau217 and CSF MTBR-tau243—declined 15% and 13.3% respectively against a rising natural history. Topline unblinded results are expected early Q1 2027.

before.summary: Kinjal Gas Ltd is presenting a corporate overview ahead of a reverse takeover (RTO) into a listed Canadian vehicle, positioning itself to become the largest independent gas producer in Mexico. The transaction includes acquiring a 49% interest in the Mision gas field, farm-ins on the A10CS/CS06 blocks, and the purchase of Tonalli, with production targeted to grow to over 90 MMcf/d net within 2–3 years. The company has secured a debt facility of up to US$30 million and plans an equity financing of C$37 million to fund the acquisitions.
before.context: This transaction would make Kinjal the largest private gas operator in Mexico, with a production base of ~30 MMcf/d net and significant development upside. Comparable companies trade at EV/EBITDA multiples of 2.4x–2.9x 2026E and EV/boe/d of ~$28,000–$38,000, while Kinjal's implied metrics are significantly lower, suggesting potential re-rating.

before.grade_commentary: These are exceptional grades for a heavy mineral placer deposit. TiO2 of 10.75-17.16% over 2.7m is extremely high—most commercial mineral sand deposits grade 1-5% heavy mineral, with rutile grades often 20-60% within the concentrate. The 0.784-1.324% TREO is also notable, especially the 0.205-0.347% MREO (magnetic rare earths), which are critical for permanent magnets. The 0.7-1.2% monazite and 5.7-9.7% zircon grades are strong. True thickness is estimated at ~100% of downhole thickness (near-vertical holes), so widths are representative. High grades over narrow widths (1.2m) may require selective mining, but the broader 2.7m intersection and potential thickening to the east support bulk mining potential.

before.summary: Tusker Minerals announced a JORC (2012) Exploration Target of 2.1–2.6 billion tonnes at 2.1–2.3% THM for its Douala Basin Project in Cameroon, including 0.3–0.35% rutile and 0.06–0.07% zircon. This positions Douala among the world's largest undeveloped rutile-bearing mineral sands systems, with additional higher-grade reconnaissance drilling intersected near-surface rutile up to 0.76% rutile.
before.context: Douala's 7–8 Mt contained rutile compares to Donald's ~9.8 Mt and Kasiya's ~20 Mt, but at Exploration Target stage; it exceeds Moma's ~3.3 Mt and Thunderbird's ~2 Mt. The 0.76% rutile intercept is ~2.1x the upper end of the target range (0.35%), highlighting upside.
before.grade_commentary:
The Exploration Target grades of 0.3–0.35% rutile are moderate for a mineral sands deposit, but reconnaissance drilling returned much higher grades (up to 0.86% rutile in a 1m sample), which is exceptional for near-surface auger drilling.

However, the target is conceptual and dependent on metallurgical recovery; rutile content of ~15% of THM is high relative to ilmenite, indicating premium feedstock, but the presence of 70% kyanite poses both opportunity and processing complexity. No economic value assigned to kyanite yet.

Widths are all near-surface (0–9m), and no deeper drilling has been done below ~18–24m, so the target remains open at depth.
before.what_to_watch: Tusker intends to advance toward a maiden JORC Mineral Resource Estimate on priority zones within 6–9 months, pending drilling, permitting, and assays. Also watch for additional reconnaissance results from other targets within the 2,580 km² project area, and any funding or partnership announcements to support drilling.

before.grade_commentary: These grades are moderate for gold (mostly 1.4–2.75 g/t Au, with a peak of 2.75 g/t Au), which is not exceptional for orogenic gold systems but is consistent with the lower-grade envelope surrounding potential high-grade shoots. The significance lies in the continuity and extension of the mineralised trend, not the absolute grades. Intercepts are from air core drilling with true widths estimated at 70-80% of downhole intervals, so the true widths are relatively narrow (approximately 0.7-2.4m).

before.summary: Vantage Metals (formerly Belararox, ASX: VAN) ended the June 2026 quarter with A$2.46M cash and zero debt after raising A$6M from strategic investors, but has only ~0.6 quarters of funding, with A$1M due to be released in July after shareholder approval. The company mobilized a diamond drill rig (via Major Drilling affiliate Rots) to start its first drilling program at the Kalahari Copper Project in Botswana, following AEM and ionic soil surveys that identified priority targets on the prospective D'Kar–Ngwako Pan contact. At the TMT project in Argentina, drilling returned narrow high-grade silver-zinc-copper-gold intercepts at Toro Central, including 1.75m @ 312 g/t Ag, 25.4% Zn, 2.24% Cu, 0.17 g/t Au.
before.context: Vantage's Kalahari Copper Project is located within 100 km of MMG's Khoemacau copper hub (production ~50kt Cu/yr, expanding to 130kt). The AEM survey confirmed geological continuity of the prospective D'Kar–Ngwako Pan contact into the company's tenure, targeting a sediment-hosted copper-silver belt. The Toro Central intercept of 312 g/t Ag, 25.4% Zn is exceptionally high-grade but the 1.75m width suggests a narrow epithermal vein; such grades can be economic if true widths are sufficient and metallurgy is amenable, but the company notes that recent holes have not yet replicated the outstanding high-grade interval from TMT-TC-DDH-002.

before.summary: Sunshine Metals has commenced a 4,528m RC drilling program at the Sybil epithermal gold project, part of the Ravenswood Consolidated Project in Queensland. Drilling is targeting three areas—Francis Creek, Francis Creek East, and Blue Range—with results expected from August to October 2026. The program follows a 2025 diamond drilling campaign at Francis Creek that returned multiple high-grade gold intercepts.
before.grade_commentary: The 2025 results reported in this filing are exceptional: 4.4m @ 57.51 g/t Au (bonanza grade >10 g/t Au) and 0.5m @ 19.9 g/t Au (bonanza), with downhole widths only—no true widths reported. These grades are well above epithermal averages and indicate a high-grade system, but the narrow widths suggest selective mining may be required if economic.
